# Phase 4.10 Wave 2 — closing megaudit

Audit the 7-commit arc W5-163 → W5-169 that closed Function Library Wave 2.

## Background

Wave 2 added 44 functions across 7 batches per the W5-162.1 design doc v2 (which had its own Codex pre-review applied; 3 HIGH + 4 MEDIUM closed BEFORE implementation). Each batch shipped with unit tests + e2e + matrix update; all 7 gates green per commit.

Commits to audit (in order):
- `1617e5570eb` W5-163 / 4.10.A — Logical fillins: IFS, IFNA, XOR, SWITCH
- `9832322ed13` W5-164 / 4.10.B — Conditional aggregates: MINIFS, MAXIFS, COUNTBLANK
- `152209a760e` W5-165 / 4.10.C — *A variants + info scalars: AVERAGEA/MAXA/MINA + NA/ERROR.TYPE/TYPE/ISEVEN/ISODD/ISNONTEXT/N
- `da9df6073a3` W5-166 / 4.10.D — Combinatorics + sum-of-squares: FACT/FACTDOUBLE/COMBIN/COMBINA/PERMUT/PERMUTATIONA/SUMSQ + SUMX2MY2/SUMX2PY2/SUMXMY2
- `640f819e5d4` W5-167 / 4.10.E — Text utilities: CHAR/CODE/UNICODE/UNICHAR + VALUE/FIXED/DOLLAR + TEXTJOIN
- `f27f2492a98` W5-168 / 4.10.F — Financial: PMT/FV/PV/NPER/RATE/IPMT/PPMT + NPV/IRR (new module `financial_fns.rs`)
- `2d269f84faf` W5-169 / 4.10.G — Modern lookups + ADDRESS: XLOOKUP/XMATCH + ADDRESS

Total: 44 new functions, +228 workspace tests (2643 → 2838).

## Specific review asks

1. **Excel canon correctness** — pick 3-5 functions you suspect might diverge from Excel canon and verify them against the IronCalc references at `.references/ironcalc/base/src/functions/` AND against Microsoft's official documentation. Specifically scrutinize:
   - SWITCH type-strictness + error propagation (already corrected per Codex HIGH-1 in W5-162.1, but verify the test suite covers it).
   - RATE / IRR Newton-Raphson behavior: tolerance + iteration cap match IronCalc.
   - PMT / FV / PV / NPER / IPMT / PPMT TVM equation matches IronCalc exactly.
   - NPV / IRR non-numeric handling: NPV skips, IRR rejects with #VALUE!.
   - XLOOKUP next-smaller / next-larger semantics on UNSORTED data: my impl tracks best candidate during linear scan — is that what Excel does, or does Excel assume sorted input?
   - ADDRESS sheet quoting rules: I quote if anything outside `[A-Za-z0-9_]`; Excel's actual rule is more nuanced (only quotes if starts with digit, contains certain chars, etc.).

2. **Cross-cutting consistency** — do all 44 new functions handle these the same way?
   - Empty arg list (some return #VALUE!, some might return #DIV/0!).
   - Errors in args (all should propagate; check for any that silently swallow).
   - Blank arg (coerced to 0 for math, "" for text — consistent?).
   - Wrong arity (all #VALUE!).

3. **Numerical stability** — RATE / IRR use Newton-Raphson. Specific concerns:
   - Does RATE handle near-zero rate gracefully? IronCalc has `rate == 0` short-circuit; I do too — verify.
   - Does IRR's bisection fallback correctly handle cash flows where N-R diverges?
   - Are the eps values (1e-7 for RATE, 1e-8 / 1e-10 for IRR) reasonable vs Excel's ~1e-9?

4. **Matrix accuracy** — `docs/compat/excel-matrix.md` was updated batch-by-batch. Any rows still tagged ❌ that should now be ✅? Any test-count fields outdated? Any rows where the Notes column is misleading?

5. **Test coverage gaps** — for each batch, what scenarios are NOT covered that should be? Examples to consider:
   - Negative `decimals` for FIXED with thousands grouping turned off.
   - DOLLAR with negative decimals.
   - XLOOKUP if_not_found = a Range arg (my code returns #VALUE! — is that right?).
   - ADDRESS with sheet name containing single quotes (does my doubling rule work?).
   - Combinatoric overflow boundaries beyond what tests check.

6. **Stale docstrings / comments anywhere** referencing "Wave 2 deferred" or "shipped 4.5" when 4.10.E text utilities now cover it.

7. **Module / file structure** — `financial_fns.rs` was added as a new module. Should anything in it be promoted to a shared `num_iter.rs` per the W5-162.1 § 5 design ("Iterative-numeric helpers (W5-168 design § 5)")? Or is the current inline placement fine?

8. **Memory / handoff doc** — `~/.claude/projects/.../memory/quantbook_engine_session_2026_05_14_handoff.md` may be stale relative to Wave 2 closure. Worth refreshing?

Report findings as HIGH / MEDIUM / LOW with file:line, contract violated, and proposed fix. Be terse but specific. If you disagree with implementation choices, say so plainly. This is the closing megaudit — be thorough.

docs/audits/2026-05-13-w5-61-megaudit-sonnet.md:49:`crates/ql-functions/src/range_fns.rs:1375-1397`. Excel's CONCAT (and its sibling TEXTJOIN) enforce a 32,767-character cap on the output and return `#VALUE!` when exceeded. REPT in this codebase already enforces this cap (`scalar_fns.rs:1841: if target_len > 32_767`). CONCAT just appends to `out` unbounded. A user who calls `CONCAT(A1:Z1000)` on a sheet of long text cells gets a multi-megabyte string instead of `#VALUE!`. Excel canon diverges. No test pins this either way.

Default decimals=2; negative decimals round LEFT of decimal point; `no_commas=TRUE` suppresses grouping. Half-away-from-zero rounding. Locale-aware separators (EnUs: `,` thousands `.` decimal; De: `.` thousands `,` decimal; Fr: ` ` thousands `,` decimal). |
docs/compat/excel-matrix.md:180:| DOLLAR | ✅ | 3 | 4.10.E | W5-167: currency text with `$` prefix. ContextAwareFn. Always groups thousands. Negatives → `-$1,234.50` (V1 — accounting parens + locale-specific currency symbol deferred to Phase 4.5 polish). |
docs/compat/excel-matrix.md:181:| CHAR / CODE | ✅ | 5 | 4.10.E | W5-167: codepoint round-trip for code 1..=255. **DIVERGENCE**: Excel uses Windows-1252; we use Unicode codepoint mapping. Identical for 1-127 ASCII; positions 128-159 differ (Windows-1252 has extra glyphs; Unicode has C1 control characters). Document divergence; bundle Windows-1252 polish with deferred UTF-16 work. |
docs/compat/excel-matrix.md:182:| UNICODE / UNICHAR | ✅ | 5 | 4.10.E | W5-167: full Unicode codepoint round-trip. UNICHAR: code 1..=char::MAX; surrogates (0xD800..=0xDFFF) → #N/A. Canonical match vs Excel. |
docs/compat/excel-matrix.md:208:| XLOOKUP | ✅ | 10 | 4.10.G | W5-169: scalar-return V1. Modes: match_mode (0=exact, -1=exact-or-next-smaller, 1=exact-or-next-larger, 2=wildcard); search_mode (1=forward, -1=reverse, ±2=binary — V1 uses linear scan, same result, no perf advantage). `if_not_found` arg returned on miss (default `#N/A`). lookup_array must be 1D; 2D return_array → `#VALUE!` (spill semantics await Phase 4.7 polish). |
docs/compat/excel-matrix.md:210:| XMATCH | ✅ | 4 | 4.10.G | W5-169: modern MATCH variant. Returns 1-based position; same match_mode + search_mode semantics as XLOOKUP. No match → `#N/A`. |
docs/compat/excel-matrix.md:214:| ADDRESS | ✅ | 8 | 4.10.G | W5-169: cell address text formatter. `abs_num`: 1=$A$1 (default), 2=A$1, 3=$A1, 4=A1. `a1`: TRUE → A1 style (default), FALSE → R1C1. `sheet_text`: optional prefix; auto-quoted if it contains anything other than `[A-Za-z0-9_]`. row/col must be ≥ 1 → otherwise `#VALUE!`. Multi-letter columns supported (Z, AA, ZZ, AAA). |
docs/compat/excel-matrix.md:234:| ISEVEN / ISODD | ✅ | 4 | 4.10.C | W5-165: truncate toward zero (matches Excel canon — `ISEVEN(-2.5)` truncates to -2 → even). Blank coerces to 0 → ISEVEN(blank) = TRUE. Text → #VALUE!. |
docs/compat/excel-matrix.md:235:| ISNONTEXT | ✅ | 1 | 4.10.C | W5-165: inverse of ISTEXT. Blank / Number / Boolean / Error → TRUE; only Text → FALSE. |
docs/compat/excel-matrix.md:236:| TYPE | ✅ | 1 | 4.10.C | W5-165: 1=Number (Blank also coerces to 1), 2=Text, 4=Boolean, 16=Error. Excel's 64=Array unreachable on this scalar path; flattening happens in eval dispatch. |
docs/compat/excel-matrix.md:237:| N | ✅ | 2 | 4.10.C | W5-165: Number → same; Blank → 0; Boolean → 1/0; **Text → 0 (NOT `#VALUE!` per Excel canon; verified vs IronCalc)**; Error → propagate. Date values (stored as Number) round-trip identically. |
docs/compat/excel-matrix.md:238:| NA | ✅ | 2 | 4.10.C | W5-165: arity 0 → `#N/A`. Args → `#VALUE!`. |
docs/compat/excel-matrix.md:239:| ERROR.TYPE | ✅ | 3 | 4.10.C | W5-165: 1=#NULL!, 2=#DIV/0!, 3=#VALUE!, 4=#REF!, 5=#NAME?, 6=#NUM!, 7=#N/A. Non-error → #N/A. Quantbook-specific sigils (#SPILL!, #CALC!, #DISCONNECTED!, #BINDING!, #TIMEOUT!) get extension codes 8-12. |
docs/compat/excel-matrix.md:248:| PMT / FV / PV / NPER | ✅ | 9 | 4.10.F | W5-168: TVM equation `pv*(1+rate)^nper + pmt*(1+rate*type)*((1+rate)^nper - 1)/rate + fv = 0` (rate≠0); `pmt*nper + pv + fv = 0` (rate=0). `type=0` end of period; `type=1` (or any nonzero) beginning. Sign convention: outflows negative. Verified against IronCalc references. Returns `#NUM!` on undefined inputs (rate ≤ -1, NaN/Inf results). |
docs/compat/excel-matrix.md:249:| RATE | ✅ | 1 | 4.10.F | W5-168: Newton-Raphson, 50 iterations max, eps=1e-7. Guess defaults to 0.1 (Excel canon). Fails to converge → `#NUM!`. Initial guess ≤ -1 → `#VALUE!`. |
docs/compat/excel-matrix.md:250:| IPMT / PPMT | ✅ | 3 | 4.10.F | W5-168: interest + principal portions of period `k` payment. Invariant: `IPMT(k) + PPMT(k) = PMT`. Period < 1 or > nper+1 → `#NUM!`. |
docs/compat/excel-matrix.md:251:| NPV | ✅ | 5 | 4.10.F | W5-168: Σ values[i] / (1+rate)^(i+1) (values are END-of-period cash flows; first value discounted). Variadic — accepts scalar + range args; ranges flatten row-major. Per Excel canon: non-numeric cells (text, bool) SKIPPED, blanks skipped, errors propagate. Empty cash-flow → `#NUM!`. |
docs/compat/excel-matrix.md:252:| IRR | ✅ | 6 | 4.10.F | W5-168: Newton-Raphson around guess (default 0.1), bisection fallback over `[-0.99999, 100]`, 50 iterations max, eps=1e-8 / 1e-10. Requires sign-change in cash-flow → otherwise `#NUM!`. Non-numeric cells in range → `#VALUE!` (stricter than NPV per IronCalc canon). |
docs/compat/excel-matrix.md:253:| XNPV / XIRR / MIRR | ❌ | 0 | Wave 3 | Date-indexed variants; bundle with Wave 3 reference-tier / extended date arithmetic. |
docs/compat/excel-matrix.md:258:| Currency / formatted (DOLLAR, etc.) | ❌ | 0 | 4.5 | Display-level; depends on TEXT/format parser |
docs/compat/excel-matrix.md:352:| Dynamic-array functions (XLOOKUP, FILTER, etc.) | ❌ | 4.7 | |

docs/audits/2026-05-12-phase-2B.md:68:**Disposition:** **FIXED** in this audit-closure commit. New `RuntimeError::InvalidChunkRows(u32)` and `RuntimeError::TooManySheets { current, max }` variants. `add_sheet` pre-validates BEFORE the op log append. Tests added: `add_sheet_rejects_zero_chunk_rows`.
docs/audits/2026-05-12-phase-2B.md:77:**Disposition:** **FIXED** in this audit-closure commit. Pre-flight `NameTable::would_accept(name)` check (new pub method on ql-storage) makes the workbook mutation infallible at this layer. Ordering is now validate → append → mutate, matching the rest of the producer surface (set_value, set_formula, clear_formula, add_sheet).
docs/audits/2026-05-12-phase-2B.md:86:**Disposition:** **FIXED** in this audit-closure commit. When both ops are needed, they're now wrapped in a single `Op::BatchCommit { ops: [PutValue, ClearFormula] }` — a single Loro append, atomic. Replay treats BatchCommit as a sequence (existing semantics), so the inner-op order is preserved.
docs/audits/2026-05-12-phase-2B.md:95:**Disposition:** **FIXED** in this audit-closure commit. Commit is now reordered: build `log_ops`, append `BatchCommit` first (with `had_formula` snapshotted from pre-mutation state), THEN run pass 1 and pass 2. Workbook stays unchanged on append failure.
docs/audits/2026-05-12-phase-2B.md:103:**Disposition:** **FIXED** in this audit-closure commit. New `_assert_engine_state_is_send_sync` compile-time check in `ql-exec/src/lib.rs`. Today's Loro 1.12.0 LoroDoc satisfies both bounds; the check pins the invariant going forward.

docs/audits/2026-05-16-phase-4.10-pre-review-codex.md:174:- Errors in `expression` propagate. Errors in `valueK` skip that pair (NOT propagate — matches Excel SWITCH canon, unlike IFS which propagates test errors).
docs/audits/2026-05-16-phase-4.10-pre-review-codex.md:196:`values_match_for_switch`: case-insensitive String equality, Number/Bool/Blank exact, Error never matches. Open question for Codex pre-review: does Excel allow Number↔String cross-type match (e.g., `SWITCH(1, "1", "match")`)? IronCalc reference says NO (strict type); HyperFormula says YES (coerce). docs/audits/2026-05-16-phase-4.10-pre-review-codex.md:234:- **SWITCH** type-strictness: see § 3.1 open question. Default strict; document in matrix.
docs/audits/2026-05-16-phase-4.10-pre-review-codex.md:240:### 4.10.B — Conditional aggregate fillins (MINIFS, MAXIFS, COUNTBLANK)
docs/audits/2026-05-16-phase-4.10-pre-review-codex.md:242:Mirror W5-55 SUMIFS/COUNTIFS pattern. All `RangeAwareFn`. COUNTBLANK is simpler (single range, count blanks). MINIFS/MAXIFS share W5-55's criterion-predicate suite + W5-61 wildcards. **W5-60 KNOWN DIVERGENCE** applies (sum_range vs range shape) — surface in matrix Notes.
docs/audits/2026-05-16-phase-4.10-pre-review-codex.md:244:### 4.10.C — Stats `*A` variants (AVERAGEA, MAXA, MINA)
docs/audits/2026-05-16-phase-4.10-pre-review-codex.md:261:- `SUMSQ`, `SUMX2MY2`, `SUMX2PY2`, `SUMXMY2` — variadic sum-of-squares + cross products. RangeAwareFn for the multi-range pair variants.
docs/audits/2026-05-16-phase-4.10-pre-review-codex.md:265:- `TEXTJOIN(delim, ignore_empty, args...)` — RangeAwareFn; supersedes CONCAT for the delimiter-controlled case.
docs/audits/2026-05-16-phase-4.10-pre-review-codex.md:268:- `FIXED(number, decimals, no_commas)` — number → text with thousands grouping. Locale-aware.
docs/audits/2026-05-16-phase-4.10-pre-review-codex.md:269:- `DOLLAR(number, decimals)` — currency text. Locale-aware.
docs/audits/2026-05-16-phase-4.10-pre-review-codex.md:273:`PMT / FV / PV / NPER / RATE` — TVM family. Closed-form for PMT/FV/PV/NPER; RATE is iterative (Newton-Raphson with bounded iterations).
docs/audits/2026-05-16-phase-4.10-pre-review-codex.md:275:`NPV / IRR` — RangeAwareFn over cash-flow range. IRR is iterative.
docs/audits/2026-05-16-phase-4.10-pre-review-codex.md:281:The big one. **XLOOKUP** is the modern replacement for VLOOKUP/HLOOKUP/INDEX+MATCH. Supports 2-way lookup, multiple match modes (exact / next-larger / next-smaller / wildcard / regex-ish), search direction (first/last). RangeAwareFn.
docs/audits/2026-05-16-phase-4.10-pre-review-codex.md:283:**XMATCH** — like XLOOKUP but returns position.
docs/audits/2026-05-16-phase-4.10-pre-review-codex.md:287:**ADDRESS** — coord → A1 text. Scalar; depends on locale (R1C1 mode) — ContextAwareFn.
docs/audits/2026-05-16-phase-4.10-pre-review-codex.md:296:- **Locale-aware VALUE / FIXED / DOLLAR** (4.10.F): use existing `EvalContext.locale` (already wired in W5-153). No new infra.
docs/audits/2026-05-16-phase-4.10-pre-review-codex.md:297:- **Iterative-numeric helpers** (4.10.G RATE, IRR): a new `num_iter` module with Newton-Raphson + bounded iterations + tolerance configurable via a registry constant. Reusable.
docs/audits/2026-05-16-phase-4.10-pre-review-codex.md:307:1. **SWITCH type-strictness** (§ 3.1) — IronCalc strict vs HyperFormula lenient. Default strict; verify with reference reads.
docs/audits/2026-05-16-phase-4.10-pre-review-codex.md:310:4. **Financial canon coverage** (§ 4.10.G) — Excel's PMT formula has multiple sign-convention modes (`type` arg = 0 or 1 for begin/end of period). Confirm we match Excel exactly.

docs/audits/2026-05-16-phase-4.10-pre-review-codex.md:7755:- `SWITCH` design should change before implementation. Excel appears type-strict for number-vs-text matching: `SWITCH(1,"1","Text",1,"Number")` returns the numeric match, not the text one. IronCalc is also strict: `compare_values` ranks Number vs String as non-equal in [.references/ironcalc/base/src/functions/util.rs](/Users/sanzhar/Documents/Sanzhar/Sanzhar/quantlab/quantlab-quantbook/quantbook-engine/.references/ironcalc/base/src/functions/util.rs:51). Also fix the doc’s error rule: IronCalc propagates errored case values, it does not skip them, in [.references/ironcalc/base/src/functions/logical/switch.rs](/Users/sanzhar/Documents/Sanzhar/Sanzhar/quantlab/quantlab-quantbook/quantbook-engine/.references/ironcalc/base/src/functions/logical/switch.rs:24). Microsoft’s SWITCH page confirms exact value matching and no-match `#N/A`; a concrete Excel example for `1` vs `"1"` is here: https://www.getelyxai.com/en/excel-formulas/logical/switch.
docs/audits/2026-05-16-phase-4.10-pre-review-codex.md:7757:- Reference-tier work should be broken out as its own design doc, not hidden inside 4.10.D. Current `FnArg` carries only `Scalar` or flattened `Range`, with no address/provenance handle in [range_aware_fns.rs](/Users/sanzhar/Documents/Sanzhar/Sanzhar/quantlab/quantlab-quantbook/quantbook-engine/crates/ql-functions/src/range_aware_fns.rs:86). Smallest footprint: ship scalar info funcs first; create a small “ReferenceArg/ReferenceAwareFn” mini-phase for `ISFORMULA`, `FORMULATEXT`, `ROW/COLUMN`, `ROWS/COLUMNS`, and maybe `ADDRESS`.
docs/audits/2026-05-16-phase-4.10-pre-review-codex.md:7763:- Financial scope is undercut. The matrix says TVM includes `IPMT`/`PPMT`, and cash-flow includes `XNPV`/`XIRR`/`MIRR`; the doc only includes `PMT/FV/PV/NPER/RATE/NPV/IRR`. Either explicitly defer the missing ones or add `IPMT`/`PPMT` to 4.10.G. IronCalc’s sign convention is standard Excel TVM: `pv*(1+rate)^nper + pmt*(1+rate*type)*... + fv = 0`; `type=0` end, `type=1` beginning, with nonzero type treated as begin in [.references/ironcalc/base/src/functions/financial.rs](/Users/sanzhar/Documents/Sanzhar/Sanzhar/quantlab/quantlab-quantbook/quantbook-engine/.references/ironcalc/base/src/functions/financial.rs:176).

   442	///   silently discarded (no match found → still `#N/A`; matches
   443	///   Excel canon, not a syntax error).
   444	/// - Empty input → `#VALUE!`.
   445	pub fn ifs(args: &[Value]) -> Value {

   447	        return Value::Error(ErrorValue::Value);
   448	    }

   453	            other => match coercion::to_logical(other) {
   454	                Ok(true) => return args[i + 1].clone(),
   455	                Ok(false) => {}
   456	                Err(e) => return Value::Error(e),
   457	            },
   458	        }
   459	        i += 2;
   460	    }
   461	    Value::Error(ErrorValue::NA)
   462	}

   464	/// **W5-163 (Phase 4.10.A):** `XOR(args...)` — variadic logical XOR;

   466	/// arg handling: skip blanks, coerce non-bool via `to_logical`,
   467	/// propagate errors, require ≥1 non-blank → otherwise `#VALUE!`.
   468	pub fn xor(args: &[Value]) -> Value {

   470	        return Value::Error(ErrorValue::Value);
   471	    }

   473	    let mut any_non_blank = false;

   475	        match v {
   476	            Value::Error(e) => return Value::Error(*e),
   477	            Value::Blank => {}
   478	            other => {
   479	                any_non_blank = true;
   480	                match coercion::to_logical(other) {
   481	                    Ok(true) => count += 1,
   482	                    Ok(false) => {}
   483	                    Err(e) => return Value::Error(e),
   484	                }
   485	            }
   486	        }
   487	    }
   488	    if !any_non_blank {
   489	        return Value::Error(ErrorValue::Value);
   490	    }

   495	/// value2, result2, ..., [default])` — value-matching selector.
   496	///
   497	/// Per Excel canon + Codex pre-review (verified against IronCalc
   498	/// `compare_values` + `logical/switch.rs` + Microsoft docs):
   499	/// - **Type-strict equality**: Number ≠ "1" (Number↔String never
   500	///   match). NaN never matches NaN.
   501	/// - **Errors in caseK values PROPAGATE** (NOT skipped — corrects
   502	///   the v1 design-doc draft).
   503	/// - Errors in `expression` propagate.
   504	/// - Variadic ≥3 args (1 expression + at least 1 value+result pair).
   505	/// - Even args after expression → no default → `#N/A` on no match.
   506	/// - Odd args after expression → trailing unpaired arg is the
   507	///   default.
   508	pub fn switch(args: &[Value]) -> Value {
   509	    if args.len() < 3 {
   510	        return Value::Error(ErrorValue::Value);
   511	    }
   512	    let expr = &args[0];
   513	    if let Value::Error(e) = expr {
   514	        return Value::Error(*e);
   515	    }
   516	    let mut i = 1;
   517	    while i + 1 < args.len() {
   518	        let v = &args[i];
   519	        // Codex HIGH-1: errors in caseK PROPAGATE before the no-match
   520	        // → #N/A path runs.
   521	        if let Value::Error(e) = v {
   522	            return Value::Error(*e);
   523	        }
   524	        if values_match_strict(expr, v) {
   525	            return args[i + 1].clone();
   526	        }
   527	        i += 2;
   528	    }
   529	    // i == args.len() - 1 → trailing unpaired arg is the default.
   530	    if i < args.len() {
   531	        return args[i].clone();
   532	    }
   533	    Value::Error(ErrorValue::NA)
   534	}

   536	/// **W5-163 (Phase 4.10.A):** type-strict equality used by `SWITCH`.
   537	/// - Number == Number iff bitwise equal (NaN never matches anything).
   538	/// - Boolean == Boolean iff exact.
   539	/// - String == String iff case-INsensitive ASCII equal (matches
   540	///   Excel canon; Unicode case-folding awaits the deferred UTF-16
   541	///   work tracked in the matrix).
   542	/// - Blank == Blank.
   543	/// - Cross-type (Number↔String, Bool↔Number, Bool↔String, etc.) →
   544	///   never matches.
   545	/// - Error values handled upstream; this helper assumes both sides
   546	///   are non-error.
   547	fn values_match_strict(a: &Value, b: &Value) -> bool {
   548	    match (a, b) {
   549	        (Value::Number(x), Value::Number(y)) => x.to_bits() == y.to_bits() && !x.is_nan(),
   550	        (Value::Boolean(x), Value::Boolean(y)) => x == y,
   551	        (Value::Text(x), Value::Text(y)) => x.eq_ignore_ascii_case(y),
   552	        (Value::Blank, Value::Blank) => true,
   553	        _ => false,
   554	    }
   555	}

   559	/// `ABS(x)` — absolute value.
   560	pub fn abs(args: &[Value]) -> Value {
   561	    if args.len() != 1 {
   562	        return Value::Error(ErrorValue::Value);
   563	    }
   564	    match coerce_numeric(&args[0]) {
   565	        NumericArg::Number(n) => Value::Number(n.abs()),
   566	        NumericArg::Skip => Value::Number(0.0),
   567	        NumericArg::Error(e) => Value::Error(e),
   568	    }
   569	}

     2	//!
     3	//! TVM family (PMT, FV, PV, NPER, RATE, IPMT, PPMT) + cash-flow

     7	//!
     8	//! ## TVM equation
     9	//!
    10	//! ```text
    11	//! pv * (1+rate)^nper
    12	//!   + pmt * (1+rate*type) * ((1+rate)^nper - 1) / rate
    13	//!   + fv = 0                                  // rate != 0
    14	//!
    15	//! pmt * nper + pv + fv = 0                    // rate == 0
    16	//! ```
    17	//!
    18	//! - `type = 0` → payments at END of period (default).
    19	//! - `type = 1` → payments at BEGINNING of period.
    20	//! - Per Excel canon: any non-zero `type` is treated as `1`.
    21	//!
    22	//! ## Sign convention
    23	//!
    24	//! Outflows are negative, inflows positive. `PMT(loan)` returns a
    25	//! negative number (money you pay out). Matches Excel + IronCalc.

    31	// ===== Argument helpers =====
    32	
    33	/// Coerce an arg into a number. Blank → 0. Errors propagate.
    34	fn arg_num(v: &Value) -> Result<f64, ErrorValue> {
    35	    match coerce_numeric(v) {
    36	        NumericArg::Number(n) => Ok(n),
    37	        NumericArg::Skip => Ok(0.0),
    38	        NumericArg::Error(e) => Err(e),
    39	    }
    40	}
    41	
    42	/// Coerce optional `type` arg into the `period_start` bool. Per Excel:
    43	/// any non-zero value is treated as TRUE (period start).
    44	fn arg_type(v: &Value) -> Result<bool, ErrorValue> {
    45	    match coerce_numeric(v) {
    46	        NumericArg::Number(n) => Ok(n != 0.0),
    47	        NumericArg::Skip => Ok(false),
    48	        NumericArg::Error(e) => Err(e),
    49	    }

    52	// ===== Core TVM helpers (pure math; mirror IronCalc references) =====
    53	
    54	/// `PMT` core. Returns `Err(ErrorValue::Num)` for NaN/Inf or
    55	/// undefined inputs (rate ≤ -1).
    56	pub(crate) fn compute_payment(
    57	    rate: f64,
    58	    nper: f64,
    59	    pv: f64,
    60	    fv: f64,
    61	    period_start: bool,
    62	) -> Result<f64, ErrorValue> {
    63	    if rate == 0.0 {
    64	        if nper == 0.0 {
    65	            return Err(ErrorValue::Num);
    66	        }
    67	        return Ok(-(pv + fv) / nper);
    68	    }
    69	    if rate <= -1.0 {
    70	        return Err(ErrorValue::Num);
    71	    }
    72	    let rate_nper = if nper == 0.0 {
    73	        1.0
    74	    } else {
    75	        (1.0 + rate).powf(nper)
    76	    };
    77	    let result = if period_start {
    78	        (fv + pv * rate_nper) * rate / ((1.0 + rate) * (1.0 - rate_nper))
    79	    } else {
    80	        (fv * rate + pv * rate * rate_nper) / (1.0 - rate_nper)
    81	    };
    82	    if result.is_nan() || result.is_infinite() {
    83	        return Err(ErrorValue::Num);
    84	    }
    85	    Ok(result)
    86	}

    88	/// `FV` core.
    89	pub(crate) fn compute_future_value(
    90	    rate: f64,
    91	    nper: f64,
    92	    pmt: f64,
    93	    pv: f64,
    94	    period_start: bool,
    95	) -> Result<f64, ErrorValue> {
    96	    if rate == 0.0 {
    97	        return Ok(-pv - pmt * nper);
    98	    }
    99	    if rate == -1.0 && nper < 0.0 {
   100	        return Err(ErrorValue::DivZero);
   101	    }
   102	    let rate_nper = (1.0 + rate).powf(nper);
   103	    let fv = if period_start {
   104	        -pv * rate_nper - pmt * (1.0 + rate) * (rate_nper - 1.0) / rate
   105	    } else {
   106	        -pv * rate_nper - pmt * (rate_nper - 1.0) / rate
   107	    };
   108	    if fv.is_nan() {
   109	        return Err(ErrorValue::Num);
   110	    }
   111	    if !fv.is_finite() {
   112	        return Err(ErrorValue::DivZero);
   113	    }
   114	    Ok(fv)
   115	}

   117	/// `PV` core. Solves the TVM equation for `pv`.
   118	pub(crate) fn compute_present_value(
   119	    rate: f64,
   120	    nper: f64,
   121	    pmt: f64,
   122	    fv: f64,
   123	    period_start: bool,
   124	) -> Result<f64, ErrorValue> {
   125	    if rate == 0.0 {
   126	        return Ok(-fv - pmt * nper);
   127	    }
   128	    if rate <= -1.0 {
   129	        return Err(ErrorValue::Num);
   130	    }
   131	    let rate_nper = (1.0 + rate).powf(nper);
   132	    let annuity_factor = if period_start {
   133	        pmt * (1.0 + rate) * (rate_nper - 1.0) / rate
   134	    } else {
   135	        pmt * (rate_nper - 1.0) / rate
   136	    };
   137	    let result = -(fv + annuity_factor) / rate_nper;
   138	    if result.is_nan() || result.is_infinite() {
   139	        return Err(ErrorValue::Num);
   140	    }
   141	    Ok(result)
   142	}

   144	/// `NPER` core. Solves the TVM equation for `nper` using logarithms.
   145	/// Returns `#NUM!` when no real solution exists.
   146	pub(crate) fn compute_nper(
   147	    rate: f64,
   148	    pmt: f64,
   149	    pv: f64,
   150	    fv: f64,
   151	    period_start: bool,
   152	) -> Result<f64, ErrorValue> {
   153	    if rate == 0.0 {
   154	        if pmt == 0.0 {
   155	            return Err(ErrorValue::Num);
   156	        }
   157	        return Ok(-(pv + fv) / pmt);
   158	    }
   159	    if rate <= -1.0 {
   160	        return Err(ErrorValue::Num);
   161	    }
   162	    // pmt' = pmt * (1 + rate*type) / rate; want (1+rate)^nper * (pv + pmt') = pmt' - fv
   163	    let pmt_factor = if period_start {
   164	        pmt * (1.0 + rate) / rate
   165	    } else {
   166	        pmt / rate
   167	    };
   168	    let num = pmt_factor - fv;
   169	    let den = pv + pmt_factor;
   170	    if den == 0.0 {
   171	        return Err(ErrorValue::Num);
   172	    }
   173	    let ratio = num / den;
   174	    if ratio <= 0.0 {
   175	        return Err(ErrorValue::Num);
   176	    }
   177	    let log_base = (1.0 + rate).ln();
   178	    if log_base == 0.0 {
   179	        return Err(ErrorValue::Num);
   180	    }
   181	    let nper = ratio.ln() / log_base;
   182	    if nper.is_nan() || nper.is_infinite() {
   183	        return Err(ErrorValue::Num);
   184	    }
   185	    Ok(nper)
   186	}

   188	/// `RATE` core — Newton-Raphson with bounded iterations.
   189	/// Per IronCalc: 50 iterations, eps = 1e-7, guess > -1.
   190	pub(crate) fn compute_rate(
   191	    nper: f64,
   192	    pmt: f64,
   193	    pv: f64,
   194	    fv: f64,
   195	    period_start: bool,
   196	    guess: f64,
   197	) -> Result<f64, ErrorValue> {
   198	    if guess <= -1.0 {
   199	        return Err(ErrorValue::Value);
   200	    }
   201	    let mut rate = guess;
   202	    let max_iterations = 50;
   203	    let eps = 1e-7;
   204	    let annuity_type = if period_start { 1.0 } else { 0.0 };
   205	    for _ in 1..=max_iterations {
   206	        // f(rate) = pv*(1+r)^nper + pmt*(1+r*type)*((1+r)^nper-1)/r + fv
   207	        // f'(rate) is the derivative wrt rate.
   208	        let t = (1.0 + rate).powf(nper - 1.0);
   209	        let tt = t * (1.0 + rate);
   210	        let f = pv * tt + pmt * (1.0 + rate * annuity_type) * (tt - 1.0) / rate + fv;
   211	        let f_prime = pv * nper * t - pmt * (tt - 1.0) / (rate * rate)
   212	            + pmt * (1.0 + rate * annuity_type) * t * nper / rate;
   213	        if f_prime == 0.0 {
   214	            return Err(ErrorValue::Num);
   215	        }
   216	        let new_rate = rate - f / f_prime;
   217	        if new_rate <= -1.0 {
   218	            return Err(ErrorValue::Num);
   219	        }
   220	        if (new_rate - rate).abs() < eps {
   221	            return Ok(new_rate);
   222	        }
   223	        rate = new_rate;
   224	    }
   225	    Err(ErrorValue::Num)
   226	}

   228	/// `IPMT` core — interest portion of the `period`-th payment.
   229	pub(crate) fn compute_ipmt(
   230	    rate: f64,
   231	    period: f64,
   232	    nper: f64,
   233	    pv: f64,
   234	    fv: f64,
   235	    period_start: bool,
   236	) -> Result<f64, ErrorValue> {
   237	    let payment = compute_payment(rate, nper, pv, fv, period_start)?;
   238	    if period < 1.0 || period >= nper + 1.0 {
   239	        return Err(ErrorValue::Num);
   240	    }
   241	    if period == 1.0 && period_start {
   242	        return Ok(0.0);
   243	    }
   244	    let p = if period_start {
   245	        period - 2.0
   246	    } else {
   247	        period - 1.0
   248	    };
   249	    let c = if period_start { -payment } else { 0.0 };

   270	/// `NPV` core. Excel canon: each value is discounted by `(1+rate)^i`

   272	pub(crate) fn compute_npv(rate: f64, values: &[f64]) -> Result<f64, ErrorValue> {

   282	    }
   283	    Ok(npv)
   284	}

   657	// ===== RangeAwareFn wrappers — NPV / IRR =====
   658	
   659	/// Collect numeric values from a variadic mix of scalars + ranges.
   660	/// Non-numeric cells (text, blank) are SKIPPED per Excel NPV canon
   661	/// (matches IronCalc's `get_array_of_numbers`). Errors propagate.
   662	fn collect_cashflow(args: &[FnArg]) -> Result<Vec<f64>, ErrorValue> {
   663	    let mut out = Vec::new();
   664	    for arg in args {
   665	        match arg {
   666	            FnArg::Scalar(v) => match v {
   667	                Value::Number(n) => out.push(*n),
   668	                Value::Blank => {} // skip
   669	                Value::Error(e) => return Err(*e),
   670	                _ => {} // skip text/bool (Excel NPV canon)
   671	            },
   672	            FnArg::Range { values, .. } => {
   673	                for v in values {
   674	                    match v {
   675	                        Value::Number(n) => out.push(*n),
   676	                        Value::Blank => {} // skip
   677	                        Value::Error(e) => return Err(*e),
   678	                        _ => {} // skip text/bool
   679	                    }
   680	                }
   681	            }
   682	        }
   683	    }
   684	    Ok(out)
   685	}
   686	
   687	/// `NPV(rate, value1, [value2], ...)` — net present value.
   688	/// First arg is the discount rate; subsequent args are END-of-period
   689	/// cash flows. RangeAwareFn so range args are accepted; ranges
   690	/// flatten row-major. Empty cash-flow → `#NUM!`.
   691	pub fn npv(args: &[FnArg]) -> Value {
   692	    if args.len() < 2 {
   693	        return Value::Error(ErrorValue::Value);
   694	    }
   695	    let rate = match &args[0] {
   696	        FnArg::Scalar(v) => match arg_num(v) {
   697	            Ok(n) => n,
   698	            Err(e) => return Value::Error(e),
   699	        },
   700	        FnArg::Range { .. } => return Value::Error(ErrorValue::Value),
   701	    };
   702	    let values = match collect_cashflow(&args[1..]) {
   703	        Ok(v) => v,
   704	        Err(e) => return Value::Error(e),
   705	    };
   706	    if values.is_empty() {
   707	        return Value::Error(ErrorValue::Num);
   708	    }
   709	    finish(compute_npv(rate, &values))
   710	}
   711	
   712	/// `IRR(values, [guess=0.1])` — internal rate of return. Iterative
   713	/// (Newton-Raphson around guess; bisection fallback per IronCalc
   714	/// pattern). Cash-flow must include at least one positive and one
   715	/// negative value → otherwise `#NUM!`.
   716	pub fn irr(args: &[FnArg]) -> Value {
   717	    if !(1..=2).contains(&args.len()) {
   718	        return Value::Error(ErrorValue::Value);
   719	    }
   720	    let values = match &args[0] {
   721	        FnArg::Range { values, .. } => {
   722	            // Per IronCalc: numeric values only; non-numeric (text, bool)
   723	            // → #VALUE!. Blank → skip. Errors propagate.
   724	            let mut out = Vec::new();
   725	            for v in values {
   726	                match v {
   727	                    Value::Number(n) => out.push(*n),
   728	                    Value::Blank => {}
   729	                    Value::Error(e) => return Value::Error(*e),
   730	                    _ => return Value::Error(ErrorValue::Value),
   731	                }
   732	            }
   733	            out
   734	        }
   735	        FnArg::Scalar(_) => return Value::Error(ErrorValue::Value),
   736	    };
   737	    if values.is_empty() {
   738	        return Value::Error(ErrorValue::Num);
   739	    }
   740	    let guess = if args.len() == 2 {
   741	        match &args[1] {
   742	            FnArg::Scalar(v) => match arg_num(v) {
   743	                Ok(n) => n,
   744	                Err(e) => return Value::Error(e),
   745	            },
   746	            FnArg::Range { .. } => return Value::Error(ErrorValue::Value),
   747	        }
   748	    } else {
   749	        0.1
   750	    };
   751	    finish(compute_irr(&values, guess))
   752	}

   484	/// Decode the `search_mode` arg of XLOOKUP / XMATCH per Excel canon:
   485	/// 1=first→last (default), -1=last→first, 2=binary ascending,
   486	/// -2=binary descending. V1 implementation uses linear scan in all
   487	/// modes — the binary modes give the same RESULT but lose the perf
   488	/// advantage; document the divergence.
   489	fn decode_xlookup_search_mode(arg: Option<&FnArg>) -> Result<i32, ErrorValue> {
   490	    match arg {
   491	        None => Ok(1),
   492	        Some(FnArg::Scalar(Value::Number(n))) => {
   493	            let m = n.trunc() as i32;
   494	            if !matches!(m, 1 | -1 | 2 | -2) {
   495	                return Err(ErrorValue::Value);
   496	            }
   497	            Ok(m)
   498	        }
   499	        Some(FnArg::Scalar(Value::Blank)) => Ok(1),
   500	        Some(FnArg::Scalar(Value::Error(e))) => Err(*e),
   501	        _ => Err(ErrorValue::Value),
   502	    }
   503	}
   504	
   505	/// Wildcard match (per the existing W5-61 wildcard infrastructure):
   506	/// `?` matches any single char; `*` matches any sequence; `~` escapes.
   507	fn xlookup_wildcard_match(pattern: &Value, cell: &Value) -> bool {
   508	    let pat = match pattern {
   509	        Value::Text(s) => s.as_ref(),
   510	        _ => return lookup_eq(pattern, cell),
   511	    };
   512	    let text = match cell {
   513	        Value::Text(s) => s.as_ref(),
   514	        // Coerce non-text cells to text representation; wildcards on
   515	        // non-text are useful only when pattern is non-wildcard, in
   516	        // which case lookup_eq handles type-coercion.
   517	        _ => return lookup_eq(pattern, cell),
   518	    };
   519	    crate::wildcard::WildcardPattern::compile(pat).matches(text)
   520	}
   521	
   522	/// Find the XLOOKUP / XMATCH index per (match_mode, search_mode). Returns
   523	/// the 0-based index into `hay`, or `None` if no match.
   524	fn xlookup_find_index(
   525	    needle: &Value,
   526	    hay: &[Value],
   527	    match_mode: i32,
   528	    search_mode: i32,
   529	) -> Option<usize> {
   530	    use std::cmp::Ordering;
   531	    // Direction-aware iteration helper.
   532	    let reverse = search_mode < 0;
   533	    let indices: Box<dyn Iterator<Item = usize>> = if reverse {
   534	        Box::new((0..hay.len()).rev())
   535	    } else {
   536	        Box::new(0..hay.len())
   537	    };
   538	    let mut best_smaller: Option<usize> = None;
   539	    let mut best_larger: Option<usize> = None;
   540	    for i in indices {
   541	        let cell = &hay[i];
   542	        let eq = match match_mode {
   543	            2 => xlookup_wildcard_match(needle, cell),
   544	            _ => lookup_eq(needle, cell),
   545	        };
   546	        if eq {
   547	            return Some(i);
   548	        }
   549	        if match_mode == -1 || match_mode == 1 {
   550	            match lookup_cmp(cell, needle) {
   551	                Some(Ordering::Less) if match_mode == -1 => {
   552	                    // Track the LARGEST cell that's still < needle.
   553	                    let take = match best_smaller {
   554	                        None => true,
   555	                        Some(j) => matches!(lookup_cmp(cell, &hay[j]), Some(Ordering::Greater)),
   556	                    };
   557	                    if take {
   558	                        best_smaller = Some(i);
   559	                    }
   560	                }
   561	                Some(Ordering::Greater) if match_mode == 1 => {
   562	                    // Track the SMALLEST cell that's still > needle.
   563	                    let take = match best_larger {
   564	                        None => true,
   565	                        Some(j) => matches!(lookup_cmp(cell, &hay[j]), Some(Ordering::Less)),
   566	                    };
   567	                    if take {
   568	                        best_larger = Some(i);
   569	                    }
   570	                }
   571	                _ => {}
   572	            }
   573	        }
   574	    }
   575	    match match_mode {
   576	        -1 => best_smaller,
   577	        1 => best_larger,
   578	        _ => None,
   579	    }
   580	}
   581	
   582	/// **W5-169 (Phase 4.10.G):** `XLOOKUP(lookup_value, lookup_array,
   583	/// return_array, [if_not_found], [match_mode=0], [search_mode=1])` —
   584	/// modern replacement for VLOOKUP / HLOOKUP / INDEX+MATCH. V1 returns
   585	/// scalar results only (2D return_array → Phase 4.7 spill).
   586	///
   587	/// **Match modes** (per Excel canon):
   588	/// - `0` exact (default).
   589	/// - `-1` exact or next smaller.
   590	/// - `1` exact or next larger.
   591	/// - `2` wildcard (`?`, `*`, `~` escape).
   592	///
   593	/// **Search modes**:
   594	/// - `1` first→last (default).
   595	/// - `-1` last→first.
   596	/// - `2` binary ascending — V1 uses linear scan (same result, no
   597	///   perf advantage). Caller must pre-sort.
   598	/// - `-2` binary descending — same V1 caveat.
   599	///
   600	/// `if_not_found`: returned on no match. If omitted, `#N/A`.
   601	pub fn xlookup(args: &[FnArg]) -> Value {
   602	    if !(3..=6).contains(&args.len()) {
   603	        return Value::Error(ErrorValue::Value);
   604	    }
   605	    let needle = match &args[0] {
   606	        FnArg::Scalar(v) => v,
   607	        FnArg::Range { .. } => return Value::Error(ErrorValue::Value),
   608	    };
   609	    if let Value::Error(e) = needle {
   610	        return Value::Error(*e);
   611	    }
   612	    let (hay, hay_rows, hay_cols) = match &args[1] {
   613	        FnArg::Range { values, rows, cols } => (values.as_slice(), *rows, *cols),
   614	        FnArg::Scalar(_) => return Value::Error(ErrorValue::Value),
   615	    };
   616	    let (ret, ret_rows, ret_cols) = match &args[2] {
   617	        FnArg::Range { values, rows, cols } => (values.as_slice(), *rows, *cols),
   618	        FnArg::Scalar(_) => return Value::Error(ErrorValue::Value),
   619	    };
   620	    // V1: lookup_array must be 1D (single row OR single column) and
   621	    // return_array must have the same length. 2D return_array → Phase
   622	    // 4.7 spill.
   623	    if hay_rows != 1 && hay_cols != 1 {
   624	        return Value::Error(ErrorValue::Value);
   625	    }
   626	    if ret.len() != hay.len() {
   627	        return Value::Error(ErrorValue::Value);
   628	    }
   629	    // V1 scalar return only.
   630	    if ret_rows != 1 && ret_cols != 1 {
   631	        return Value::Error(ErrorValue::Value);
   632	    }
   633	    let match_mode = match decode_xlookup_match_mode(args.get(4)) {
   634	        Ok(m) => m,
   635	        Err(e) => return Value::Error(e),
   636	    };
   637	    let search_mode = match decode_xlookup_search_mode(args.get(5)) {
   638	        Ok(m) => m,
   639	        Err(e) => return Value::Error(e),
   640	    };
   641	    match xlookup_find_index(needle, hay, match_mode, search_mode) {
   642	        Some(i) => ret[i].clone(),
   643	        None => {
   644	            // if_not_found: clone the scalar arg if provided; else #N/A.
   645	            if let Some(arg) = args.get(3) {
   646	                match arg {
   647	                    FnArg::Scalar(v) => v.clone(),
   648	                    FnArg::Range { .. } => Value::Error(ErrorValue::Value),
   649	                }
   650	            } else {
   651	                Value::Error(ErrorValue::NA)
   652	            }
   653	        }
   654	    }
   655	}
   656	
   657	/// **W5-169 (Phase 4.10.G):** `XMATCH(lookup_value, lookup_array,
   658	/// [match_mode=0], [search_mode=1])` — modern replacement for MATCH.
   659	/// Returns the 1-based position in `lookup_array`. Same match_mode +
   660	/// search_mode semantics as `XLOOKUP`. No match → `#N/A`.
   661	pub fn xmatch(args: &[FnArg]) -> Value {
   662	    if !(2..=4).contains(&args.len()) {
   663	        return Value::Error(ErrorValue::Value);
   664	    }
   665	    let needle = match &args[0] {
   666	        FnArg::Scalar(v) => v,

    16	fn is_less_than_one_year(start_date: i64, end_date: i64) -> Result<bool, String> {
    17	    let end = from_excel_date(end_date)?;
    18	    let start = from_excel_date(start_date)?;
    19	    if end_date - start_date < 365 {
    20	        return Ok(true);
    21	    }

    23	    let start_year = start.year();
    24	    if end_year == start_year {
    25	        return Ok(true);
    26	    }
    27	    if end_year != start_year + 1 {
    28	        return Ok(false);
    29	    }
    30	    let start_month = start.month();
    31	    let end_month = end.month();
    32	    if end_month < start_month {
    33	        return Ok(true);
    34	    }
    35	    if end_month > start_month {
    36	        return Ok(false);
    37	    }
    38	    // we are one year later same month
    39	    let start_day = start.day();
    40	    let end_day = end.day();
    41	    Ok(end_day <= start_day)

    10	// Returns the interest rate per period of an annuity.
    11	// RATE is calculated by iteration (using Newton-Raphson) and can have zero or more solutions.
    12	// If the successive results of RATE do not converge to within 0.0000001 after 20 iterations,
    13	// RATE returns the #NUM! error value.

    21	    guess: f64,
    22	) -> Result<f64, (Error, String)> {
    23	    let mut rate = guess;
    24	    // Excel _claims_ to do 20 iterations, but that will have tests failing
    25	    let max_iterations = 50;
    26	    let eps = 0.0000001;
    27	    let annuity_type = annuity_type as f64;
    28	    if guess <= -1.0 {
    29	        return Err((Error::VALUE, "Rate initial guess must be > -1".to_string()));
    30	    }

    32	        let t = (1.0 + rate).powf(nper - 1.0);

    43	        }
    44	        rate = new_rate;
    45	    }

    59	// * First tries Newton-Raphson around the guess
    60	// * Failing that uses bisection and bracketing
    61	// * If that fails (no root found of the interval) uses Newton-Raphson around the edges
    62	// Values for x1, x2 and the guess for N-R are fine tuned using heuristics
    63	pub(crate) fn compute_irr(values: &[f64], guess: f64) -> Result<f64, (Error, String)> {
    64	    if guess <= -1.0 {
    65	        return Err((Error::VALUE, "Rate initial guess must be > -1".to_string()));
    66	    }
    67	    // The values cannot be all positive or all negative
    68	    if values.iter().all(|&x| x >= 0.0) || values.iter().all(|&x| x <= 0.0) {
    69	        return Err((Error::NUM, "Failed to converge".to_string()));
    70	    }
    71	    if let Ok(f) = compute_irr_newton_raphson(values, guess) {
    72	        return Ok(f);
    73	    };
    74	    // We try bisection
    75	    let max_iterations = 50;
    76	    let eps = 1e-10;
    77	    let x1 = -0.99999;
    78	    let x2 = 100.0;
    79	    let f1 = compute_npv(x1, values)?;
    80	    let f2 = compute_npv(x2, values)?;
    81	    if f1 * f2 > 0.0 {
    82	        // The root is not within the limits or there are two roots
    83	        // We try Newton-Raphson a bit above the upper limit and a bit below the lower limit
    84	        if let Ok(f) = compute_irr_newton_raphson(values, 200.0) {
    85	            return Ok(f);
    86	        };
    87	        if let Ok(f) = compute_irr_newton_raphson(values, -2.0) {
    88	            return Ok(f);
    89	        };
    90	        return Err((Error::NUM, "Failed to converge".to_string()));
    91	    }
    92	    let (mut rtb, mut dx) = if f1 < 0.0 {
    93	        (x1, x2 - x1)
    94	    } else {
    95	        (x2, x1 - x2)
    96	    };
    97	    for _ in 1..max_iterations {
    98	        dx *= 0.5;
    99	        let x_mid = rtb + dx;
   100	        let f_mid = compute_npv(x_mid, values)?;
   101	        if f_mid <= 0.0 {
   102	            rtb = x_mid;
   103	        }
   104	        if f_mid.abs() < eps || dx.abs() < eps {
   105	            return Ok(x_mid);
   106	        }
   107	    }
   108	
   109	    Err((Error::NUM, "Failed to converge".to_string()))
   110	}
   111	
   112	fn compute_npv_prime(rate: f64, values: &[f64]) -> Result<f64, (Error, String)> {
   113	    let mut npv = 0.0;
   114	    for (i, item) in values.iter().enumerate() {
   115	        npv += -item * (i as f64 + 1.0) / (1.0 + rate).powi(i as i32 + 2)
   116	    }
   117	    if npv.is_infinite() || npv.is_nan() {
   118	        return Err((Error::NUM, "NaN".to_string()));
   119	    }
   120	    Ok(npv)
   121	}
   122	
   123	fn compute_irr_newton_raphson(values: &[f64], guess: f64) -> Result<f64, (Error, String)> {
   124	    let mut irr = guess;
   125	    let max_iterations = 50;
   126	    let eps = 1e-8;
   127	    for _ in 1..=max_iterations {
   128	        let f = compute_npv(irr, values)?;
   129	        let f_prime = compute_npv_prime(irr, values)?;
   130	        let new_irr = irr - f / f_prime;
   131	        if (new_irr - irr).abs() < eps {
   132	            return Ok(new_irr);
   133	        }
   134	        irr = new_irr;
   135	    }
   136	    Err((Error::NUM, "Failed to converge".to_string()))
   137	}
   138	
   139	// Formula is:
   140	//  $$\sum_{i=1}^n\frac{v_i}{(1+r)^{\frac{(d_j-d_1)}{365}}}$$
   141	// where $v_i$ is the ith-1 value and $d_i$ is the ith-1 date
   142	pub(crate) fn compute_xnpv(
   143	    rate: f64,
   144	    values: &[f64],
   145	    dates: &[f64],
   146	) -> Result<f64, (Error, String)> {
   147	    let mut xnpv = values[0];
   148	    let d0 = dates[0];
   149	    let n = values.len();
   150	    for i in 1..n {
   151	        let vi = values[i];
   152	        let di = dates[i];
   153	        xnpv += vi / ((1.0 + rate).powf((di - d0) / 365.0))
   154	    }
   155	    if xnpv.is_infinite() || xnpv.is_nan() {
   156	        return Err((Error::NUM, "NaN".to_string()));
   157	    }
   158	    Ok(xnpv)
   159	}
   160	
   161	fn compute_xnpv_prime(rate: f64, values: &[f64], dates: &[f64]) -> Result<f64, (Error, String)> {
   162	    let mut xnpv = 0.0;
   163	    let d0 = dates[0];
   164	    let n = values.len();
   165	    for i in 1..n {
   166	        let vi = values[i];
   167	        let di = dates[i];
   168	        let ratio = (di - d0) / 365.0;
   169	        let power = (1.0 + rate).powf(ratio + 1.0);
   170	        xnpv -= vi * ratio / power;
   171	    }
   172	    if xnpv.is_infinite() || xnpv.is_nan() {
   173	        return Err((Error::NUM, "NaN".to_string()));
   174	    }
   175	    Ok(xnpv)
   176	}
   177	
   178	fn compute_xirr_newton_raphson(
   179	    values: &[f64],
   180	    dates: &[f64],
   181	    guess: f64,
   182	) -> Result<f64, (Error, String)> {
   183	    let mut xirr = guess;
   184	    let max_iterations = 100;
   185	    let eps = 1e-7;
   186	    for _ in 1..=max_iterations {
   187	        let f = compute_xnpv(xirr, values, dates)?;
   188	        let f_prime = compute_xnpv_prime(xirr, values, dates)?;
   189	        let new_xirr = xirr - f / f_prime;
   190	        if (new_xirr - xirr).abs() < eps {
   191	            return Ok(new_xirr);
   192	        }
   193	        xirr = new_xirr;
   194	    }
   195	    Err((Error::NUM, "Failed to converge".to_string()))
   196	}
   197	
   198	// NOTES:
   199	// 1. If the cash-flows (value[i] for i > 0) are always of the same sign, the function is monotonous
   200	// 3. Say (d_max, v_max) are the pair where d_max is the largest date,
   201	//    then if v_max and v_0 have different signs, it's guaranteed there is a zero
   202	// The algorithm needs to be improved but it works so far in all practical cases
   203	pub(crate) fn compute_xirr(
   204	    values: &[f64],
   205	    dates: &[f64],
   206	    guess: f64,
   207	) -> Result<f64, (Error, String)> {
   208	    if guess <= -1.0 {
   209	        return Err((Error::VALUE, "Rate initial guess must be > -1".to_string()));
   210	    }
   211	    // The values cannot be all positive or all negative
   212	    if values.iter().all(|&x| x >= 0.0) || values.iter().all(|&x| x <= 0.0) {
   213	        return Err((Error::NUM, "Failed to converge".to_string()));
   214	    }
   215	    if let Ok(f) = compute_xirr_newton_raphson(values, dates, guess) {
   216	        return Ok(f);
   217	    };
   218	    // We try bisection
   219	    let max_iterations = 50;
   220	    let eps = 1e-8;
   221	    // This will miss 0's very close to -1
   222	    let x1 = -0.9999;
   223	    let x2 = 100.0;
   224	    let f1 = compute_xnpv(x1, values, dates)?;
   225	    let f2 = compute_xnpv(x2, values, dates)?;
   226	    if f1 * f2 > 0.0 {
   227	        // The root is not within the limits (or there are two roots)
   228	        // We try Newton-Raphson above the upper limit
   229	        // (we cannot go to the left of -1)
   230	        if let Ok(f) = compute_xirr_newton_raphson(values, dates, 200.0) {
   231	            return Ok(f);
   232	        };
   233	        return Err((Error::NUM, "Failed to converge".to_string()));
   234	    }
   235	
   236	    let (mut rtb, mut dx) = if f1 < 0.0 {
   237	        (x1, x2 - x1)
   238	    } else {
   239	        (x2, x1 - x2)
   240	    };
   241	
   242	    for _ in 1..max_iterations {
   243	        dx *= 0.5;
   244	        let x_mid = rtb + dx;
   245	        let f_mid = compute_xnpv(x_mid, values, dates)?;
   246	        if f_mid <= 0.0 {
   247	            rtb = x_mid;
   248	        }
   249	        if f_mid.abs() < eps || dx.abs() < eps {
   250	            return Ok(x_mid);
   251	        }
   252	    }
   253	
   254	    Err((Error::NUM, "Failed to converge".to_string()))
   255	}

docs/architecture/2026-05-15-r1c1-locales-implicit-intersection.md:177:| 3 | **4.9.C parser** (W5-139, shipped) + **4.9.C binder** (W5-140, shipped) | **Parser (W5-139):** `Token::R1C1Ref` → intermediate `Expr::R1C1Ref { sheet, row_axis, col_axis }` (new variant) + `RangeRef::R1C1Cells` for ranges. Per-axis mixed-relativity check rejects with `ParseError::R1C1MixedRelativity`. Refined the design wording "Expr::CellRef with intermediate markers" to a new variant — keeps the 50+ `CellAddr` construction sites untouched. **Binder (W5-140):** `bind_with_context_v2` lowers `Expr::R1C1Ref` → `ExprPlan::CellRef { sheet, row, col, abs_col, abs_row }` using `BindSite::at_cell` for relative axes. Absolute axes drop straight in as `n - 1` (0-indexed). Relative axes resolve against `site.cell` (None → `BindError::R1C1RequiresAnchor`). Out-of-grid resolution → `BindError::R1C1OutOfBounds { resolved_row, resolved_col }`. The `abs_col` / `abs_row` flags on the emitted `ExprPlan::CellRef` are derived per-axis from the `AxisSpec` variant — preserves the abs/rel distinction the printer needs at 4.9.D. **Range lowering deferred** — `RangeRef::R1C1Cells` still surfaces via the existing `Expr::RangeRef(_)` `UnsupportedVariant` path (same as absolute `RangeRef::Cells`); range binding is handled by the existing aggregate-function dispatch and will fold R1C1Cells when that wave touches it. Calcgraph + printer `unreachable!()` stubs unchanged: storage canon (§ 4.4) lowers R1C1 → A1 text before fingerprint / stripe registration. |

Note: rule 7 (function-returns-array → top-left) deferred — array-returning functions in scalar context still return `#CALC!` per existing 4.7.G limit; closing megaudit (4.9.O) decides whether to bundle that with cell-boundary spill rewiring or defer to a Phase 4.10 polish item. |

docs/architecture/2026-05-16-phase-4.10-function-library-wave-2.md:5:**Effort:** 3-5 weeks per MASTER-PLAN § 4.10. This doc scopes ~30-40 functions across 7 batches in **Wave 2 PART 1**. **Wave 2 does NOT close the v1 260-function target** — Wave 3 (reference-tier, distributions, depreciation, base conversion, percentile/quartile, correlation/regression, ERF/ERFC) and Wave 4 (LET/TAKE/DROP/VSTACK/HSTACK/TOCOL/TOROW/WRAPROWS/WRAPCOLS/EXPAND modern array fns) fill the remainder. docs/architecture/2026-05-13-dates-times-formats.md:1:# Phase 4.5 Dates / Times / Number Formats — Design Decision
docs/architecture/2026-05-13-dates-times-formats.md:24:Phase 4.5 from `docs/MASTER-PLAN.md` is the last big foundational phase before user-facing surfaces (cross-sheet refs, tables, R1C1, then xlsx I/O). Three deficits in current code force it now:
docs/architecture/2026-05-13-dates-times-formats.md:63:**Stop condition** (would reverse to `Value::Date` variant): If a Phase 4.5+ function requires distinguishing "this f64 means 45810 days" from "this f64 means the literal number 45810" — there's no current pressure for this. Pin if Phase 4.7 array formulas need date-typed array elements.
docs/architecture/2026-05-13-dates-times-formats.md:74:**Excel 1900 leap-year bug**: in the 1900 system, Excel treats 1900-02-29 as a real day (serial 60). For dates `>= 1900-03-01`, this just shifts the offset by 1. The 1904 system has no such bug. Phase 4.5 functions MUST replicate the 1900-system bug (else `DATEVALUE("1900-02-29")` would error on a workbook Excel happily loaded; opens an xlsx-I/O bug class).
docs/architecture/2026-05-13-dates-times-formats.md:104:**Test hooks:** `set_test_now_secs(unix_secs)` continues to override `unix_secs`. New `set_test_utc_offset_seconds(offset)` (default 0 — UTC == local for deterministic tests) overrides the offset. In production, the default `NowProvider` implementation reads from `chrono::Local::now().offset()` OR — to avoid the `chrono` dep — calls into a small `iana_time_zone` lookup (~50 LOC dep) OR uses the libc `localtime_r` FFI. **Decision deferred to 4.5.A implementation:** prototype both and benchmark; the cheaper option wins.
docs/architecture/2026-05-13-dates-times-formats.md:124:**Problem:** The W5-63 `RangeAwareFn` parallel-table pattern handled the "function arg is a range vs scalar" distinction. But Phase 4.5 introduces a NEW distinction: some functions need **workbook context** (date system, locale, now-provider). Under the current `fn(&[Value]) -> Value` signature, `DATE`, `DATEVALUE`, `WEEKDAY`, etc., have no way to read `Workbook::date_system`.
docs/architecture/2026-05-13-dates-times-formats.md:168:The `volatile.rs` clock read stays `std::time::SystemTime` on native targets; WASM uses a host callback (see § 3.2.1). Time-zone offset acquisition is the lone "real" external dependency — `iana_time_zone` (~50 LOC, single-purpose) vs libc FFI `localtime_r` — decision deferred to 4.5.A implementation per § 3.2.1.

docs/audits/2026-05-15-phase-4.9-closing-megaudit-codex-retry.md:112:## 2. Non-goals (deferred)
docs/audits/2026-05-15-phase-4.9-closing-megaudit-codex-retry.md:263:| 3 | **4.9.C parser** (W5-139, shipped) + **4.9.C binder** (W5-140, shipped) | **Parser (W5-139):** `Token::R1C1Ref` → intermediate `Expr::R1C1Ref { sheet, row_axis, col_axis }` (new variant) + `RangeRef::R1C1Cells` for ranges. Per-axis mixed-relativity check rejects with `ParseError::R1C1MixedRelativity`. Refined the design wording "Expr::CellRef with intermediate markers" to a new variant — keeps the 50+ `CellAddr` construction sites untouched. **Binder (W5-140):** `bind_with_context_v2` lowers `Expr::R1C1Ref` → `ExprPlan::CellRef { sheet, row, col, abs_col, abs_row }` using `BindSite::at_cell` for relative axes. Absolute axes drop straight in as `n - 1` (0-indexed). Relative axes resolve against `site.cell` (None → `BindError::R1C1RequiresAnchor`). Out-of-grid resolution → `BindError::R1C1OutOfBounds { resolved_row, resolved_col }`. The `abs_col` / `abs_row` flags on the emitted `ExprPlan::CellRef` are derived per-axis from the `AxisSpec` variant — preserves the abs/rel distinction the printer needs at 4.9.D. **Range lowering deferred** — `RangeRef::R1C1Cells` still surfaces via the existing `Expr::RangeRef(_)` `UnsupportedVariant` path (same as absolute `RangeRef::Cells`); range binding is handled by the existing aggregate-function dispatch and will fold R1C1Cells when that wave touches it. Calcgraph + printer `unreachable!()` stubs unchanged: storage canon (§ 4.4) lowers R1C1 → A1 text before fingerprint / stripe registration. |
docs/audits/2026-05-15-phase-4.9-closing-megaudit-codex-retry.md:272:| 12 | **4.9.L** (W5-148, shipped) | Round-trip + edge case verification suite. +12 end-to-end property tests in `workbook_runtime::tests`: mixed-relativity range rejection at set_formula, `Sales[@Col]` vs `@Sales[Qty]` semantic equivalence, `@A:A` / `@1:1` whole-range narrowing at anchor, `Sheet1!@A1` cross-sheet, R1C1+EN round-trip through op-log replay (set_reference_mode + set_formula both replayed), DE+EN round-trip through replay, `@` preservation through replay, reference_mode/locale changes leave stored text canonical, `@scalar` idempotency, `@SUM(scalar args)` no-op. Key decisions: keep `Value::Number(f64)` serial; 1900-default workbook-level date_system with 1904 alt; roll-our-own `ql-types::date` module; **new `ContextAwareFn` registry tier** (Codex HIGH 1) for date functions that need workbook context; sparse format-overlay + workbook-level `FormatTable` + 2 new op-log variants; serial-60 contract pinned per-function. 6 sub-phases planned (4.5.A.0 EvalContext tier, 4.5.A epoch+serial, 4.5.B 18-fn V1, 4.5.C 7-fn V2, 4.5.D format parser+storage+op-log, 4.5.E TEXT()+locale stubs) + mega-audit. Effort re-estimated ~6-8 sessions + 1 audit.

Refined the design wording "Expr::CellRef with intermediate markers" to a new variant — keeps the 50+ `CellAddr` construction sites untouched. **Binder (W5-140):** `bind_with_context_v2` lowers `Expr::R1C1Ref` → `ExprPlan::CellRef { sheet, row, col, abs_col, abs_row }` using `BindSite::at_cell` for relative axes. Absolute axes drop straight in as `n - 1` (0-indexed). Relative axes resolve against `site.cell` (None → `BindError::R1C1RequiresAnchor`). Calcgraph + printer `unreachable!()` stubs unchanged: storage canon (§ 4.4) lowers R1C1 → A1 text before fingerprint / stripe registration. |

ContextAwareFn. Trim whitespace; reject empty / non-numeric → #VALUE!. Numbers pass through; Blank → 0. **Strict locale-confusion guard**: in De/Fr locale, `.` in the numeric string → #VALUE! (closes ambiguity for "1.5" vs "1,5"). Currency prefixes + thousands grouping NOT parsed in V1; bundle with Phase 4.5 polish wave. |

docs/audits/2026-05-16-phase-4.10-pre-review-codex.md:281:The big one. **XLOOKUP** is the modern replacement for VLOOKUP/HLOOKUP/INDEX+MATCH. Supports 2-way lookup, multiple match modes (exact / next-larger / next-smaller / wildcard / regex-ish), search direction (first/last). RangeAwareFn.

docs/audits/2026-05-16-phase-4.10-pre-review-codex.md:616:./docs/known-gaps.md:72:| GAP-F-01 | Function library coverage — **Wave 1 (100 target) ✅ CLOSED W5-58** at 102 registry entries (≈80 unique functions + 7 aliases). Full v1 target ~260 still pending Phase 4.10 wave 2. | `ql-functions/src/registry.rs::default_registry` count | Engine | Wave 1: ✅ done. Wave 2 (≈260): Engine Phase 4.10. |
docs/audits/2026-05-16-phase-4.10-pre-review-codex.md:619:./docs/known-gaps.md:78:| GAP-F-09 | `NETWORKDAYS` holidays-array arg not supported in V1. Excel canon: 3rd arg is an optional range of holiday dates that are subtracted from the working-day count. Quantbook's `ContextAwareFn` tier signature (`fn(&[Value], &EvalContext) -> Value`) has pre-evaluated scalar args only — range args silently lose shape (or surface as `#CALC!`). Supporting holidays needs a 4th registry tier `RangeAndContextAwareFn = fn(&[FnArg], &EvalContext) -> Value`. V1: 3-arg call returns `#VALUE!`. | `crates/ql-functions/src/date_fns.rs::networkdays_ctx`; pinned by `networkdays_with_holidays_arg_is_value_error_v1_divergence` | Engine | Engine Phase 4.5.C (when tier-4 lands) or 4.7 array formulas trigger |
docs/audits/2026-05-16-phase-4.10-pre-review-codex.md:621:./docs/known-gaps.md:81:| GAP-F-07 | `FormatTable` GC / compaction not implemented. Sparse format-overlay (Phase 4.5.D) interns format strings into a workbook-level `FormatTable`. When cells change format, the old `FormatId` entry is NOT garbage-collected. Long-lived workbooks that cycle through many formats grow the table. **Decision (W5-68 design doc § 7.5):** deferred — typical workbooks don't cycle formats; a compaction pass lands in Phase 4.10 or on explicit user request. | Filed at design time (W5-68); no code yet | Engine | Engine Phase 4.10 |
docs/audits/2026-05-16-phase-4.10-pre-review-codex.md:622:./docs/known-gaps.md:82:| GAP-T-01 | Time-zone offset acquisition for `NOW()` / `TODAY()` local-time policy not implemented. Phase 4.5.A.0 EvalContext design includes a `NowProvider` trait with `utc_offset_seconds()`. The native implementation needs either a small `iana_time_zone` crate dep (~50 LOC, single-purpose) or a libc FFI `localtime_r` call. **W5-76 mega-audit closure:** `NowProvider::System` ships returning UTC offset 0 — `NOW()` / `TODAY()` are regression-neutral with the pre-W5-71 UTC path. The proper local-time hook is rescheduled from "immediate" to **Phase 4.10 polish** alongside the function-library wave 2. WASM target uses a host callback (Phase 6.3). | Filed W5-68; partial-ship in W5-71 (UTC parity); status reaffirmed W5-76 | Engine | Engine Phase 4.10 polish (was 4.5.A) |
docs/audits/2026-05-16-phase-4.10-pre-review-codex.md:623:./docs/known-gaps.md:83:| GAP-F-12 | `WorkbookRuntime::format_cache` can stale if `Workbook::formats_mut()` mutates the FormatTable AFTER `read_display` has cached the General fallback for a (then-unknown) id. The cache is keyed by `FormatId`; cache entries stay correct as long as mutations go through `WorkbookRuntime::intern_format` (the documented append-before-mutate path). Direct low-level mutation through `formats_mut()` (loader / tests only) on a live runtime is the pathological sequence. Analogous to the `WorkbookEnv` date-system staleness caveat documented at `Workbook::set_date_system`. **Decision (W5-84):** documented in the `read_display` docstring; cache-invalidation API deferred until profiling shows a real-world hit. | Filed W5-84 mega-audit closure (Codex MEDIUM-2) | Engine | Engine Phase 4.10 polish or earlier if IDE forces it |

docs/audits/2026-05-16-phase-4.10-pre-review-codex.md:822:./docs/audits/2026-05-16-phase-4.8.G.3-closing-megaudit-codex.md:2288:docs/compat/excel-matrix.md:123:| CEILING.MATH | ✅ | 7 | 4.3 polish | W5-61: signature `(number, [significance], [mode])`. Significance is `abs(significance)` — sign ignored (unlike CEILING). Default significance=1, mode=0. Positive number always rounds toward +∞; negative number with mode=0 rounds toward +∞ (toward zero), with mode≠0 rounds toward -∞ (away from zero). significance=0 returns 0. CEILING.PRECISE deferred to 4.10. |
docs/audits/2026-05-16-phase-4.10-pre-review-codex.md:823:./docs/audits/2026-05-16-phase-4.8.G.3-closing-megaudit-codex.md:2289:docs/compat/excel-matrix.md:124:| FLOOR.MATH | ✅ | 8 | 4.3 polish | W5-61: signature `(number, [significance], [mode])`. Mirror of CEILING.MATH. Positive number rounds toward -∞; negative+mode=0 toward -∞ (away from zero); negative+mode≠0 toward +∞ (toward zero). significance=0 + nonzero number → #DIV/0! (mirrors FLOOR canon, diverges from CEILING.MATH). FLOOR.PRECISE deferred to 4.10. |

docs/audits/2026-05-16-phase-4.10-pre-review-codex.md:1318:./docs/compat/excel-matrix.md:123:| CEILING.MATH | ✅ | 7 | 4.3 polish | W5-61: signature `(number, [significance], [mode])`. Significance is `abs(significance)` — sign ignored (unlike CEILING). Default significance=1, mode=0. Positive number always rounds toward +∞; negative number with mode=0 rounds toward +∞ (toward zero), with mode≠0 rounds toward -∞ (away from zero). significance=0 returns 0. CEILING.PRECISE deferred to 4.10. |
docs/audits/2026-05-16-phase-4.10-pre-review-codex.md:1319:./docs/compat/excel-matrix.md:124:| FLOOR.MATH | ✅ | 8 | 4.3 polish | W5-61: signature `(number, [significance], [mode])`. Mirror of CEILING.MATH. Positive number rounds toward -∞; negative+mode=0 toward -∞ (away from zero); negative+mode≠0 toward +∞ (toward zero). significance=0 + nonzero number → #DIV/0! (mirrors FLOOR canon, diverges from CEILING.MATH). FLOOR.PRECISE deferred to 4.10. |

Phase 4.5.A.0 EvalContext design includes a `NowProvider` trait with `utc_offset_seconds()`. The native implementation needs either a small `iana_time_zone` crate dep (~50 LOC, single-purpose) or a libc FFI `localtime_r` call. **W5-76 mega-audit closure:** `NowProvider::System` ships returning UTC offset 0 — `NOW()` / `TODAY()` are regression-neutral with the pre-W5-71 UTC path. docs/audits/2026-05-16-phase-4.10-pre-review-codex.md:1556:./docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.6-closing-megaudit-codex.txt:7357:    80	| GAP-F-12 | `WorkbookRuntime::format_cache` can stale if `Workbook::formats_mut()` mutates the FormatTable AFTER `read_display` has cached the General fallback for a (then-unknown) id. The cache is keyed by `FormatId`; cache entries stay correct as long as mutations go through `WorkbookRuntime::intern_format` (the documented append-before-mutate path). Direct low-level mutation through `formats_mut()` (loader / tests only) on a live runtime is the pathological sequence. Analogous to the `WorkbookEnv` date-system staleness caveat documented at `Workbook::set_date_system`. **Decision (W5-84):** documented in the `read_display` docstring; cache-invalidation API deferred until profiling shows a real-world hit. | Filed W5-84 mega-audit closure (Codex MEDIUM-2) | Engine | Engine Phase 4.10 polish or earlier if IDE forces it |

Significance is `abs(significance)` — sign ignored (unlike CEILING). Default significance=1, mode=0. The cache is keyed by `FormatId`; cache entries stay correct as long as mutations go through `WorkbookRuntime::intern_format` (the documented append-before-mutate path). docs/audits/2026-05-16-phase-4.8.G.3-closing-megaudit-codex.md:1714:docs/architecture/2026-05-15-r1c1-locales-implicit-intersection.md:26:## 2. Non-goals (deferred)
docs/audits/2026-05-16-phase-4.8.G.3-closing-megaudit-codex.md:1715:docs/architecture/2026-05-15-r1c1-locales-implicit-intersection.md:177:| 3 | **4.9.C parser** (W5-139, shipped) + **4.9.C binder** (W5-140, shipped) | **Parser (W5-139):** `Token::R1C1Ref` → intermediate `Expr::R1C1Ref { sheet, row_axis, col_axis }` (new variant) + `RangeRef::R1C1Cells` for ranges. Per-axis mixed-relativity check rejects with `ParseError::R1C1MixedRelativity`. Refined the design wording "Expr::CellRef with intermediate markers" to a new variant — keeps the 50+ `CellAddr` construction sites untouched. **Binder (W5-140):** `bind_with_context_v2` lowers `Expr::R1C1Ref` → `ExprPlan::CellRef { sheet, row, col, abs_col, abs_row }` using `BindSite::at_cell` for relative axes. Absolute axes drop straight in as `n - 1` (0-indexed). Relative axes resolve against `site.cell` (None → `BindError::R1C1RequiresAnchor`). Out-of-grid resolution → `BindError::R1C1OutOfBounds { resolved_row, resolved_col }`. The `abs_col` / `abs_row` flags on the emitted `ExprPlan::CellRef` are derived per-axis from the `AxisSpec` variant — preserves the abs/rel distinction the printer needs at 4.9.D. **Range lowering deferred** — `RangeRef::R1C1Cells` still surfaces via the existing `Expr::RangeRef(_)` `UnsupportedVariant` path (same as absolute `RangeRef::Cells`); range binding is handled by the existing aggregate-function dispatch and will fold R1C1Cells when that wave touches it. Calcgraph + printer `unreachable!()` stubs unchanged: storage canon (§ 4.4) lowers R1C1 → A1 text before fingerprint / stripe registration. |

docs/audits/2026-05-16-phase-4.8.G.3-closing-megaudit-codex.md:2160:docs/architecture/2026-05-13-dates-times-formats.md:104:**Test hooks:** `set_test_now_secs(unix_secs)` continues to override `unix_secs`. New `set_test_utc_offset_seconds(offset)` (default 0 — UTC == local for deterministic tests) overrides the offset. In production, the default `NowProvider` implementation reads from `chrono::Local::now().offset()` OR — to avoid the `chrono` dep — calls into a small `iana_time_zone` lookup (~50 LOC dep) OR uses the libc `localtime_r` FFI. **Decision deferred to 4.5.A implementation:** prototype both and benchmark; the cheaper option wins.
docs/audits/2026-05-16-phase-4.8.G.3-closing-megaudit-codex.md:2161:docs/architecture/2026-05-13-dates-times-formats.md:168:The `volatile.rs` clock read stays `std::time::SystemTime` on native targets; WASM uses a host callback (see § 3.2.1). Time-zone offset acquisition is the lone "real" external dependency — `iana_time_zone` (~50 LOC, single-purpose) vs libc FFI `localtime_r` — decision deferred to 4.5.A implementation per § 3.2.1.

Significance is `abs(significance)` — sign ignored (unlike CEILING). Default significance=1, mode=0. Positive number always rounds toward +∞; negative number with mode=0 rounds toward +∞ (toward zero), with mode≠0 rounds toward -∞ (away from zero). significance=0 returns 0. docs/audits/2026-05-16-phase-4.8.G.3-closing-megaudit-codex.md:2392:docs/audits/2026-05-15-phase-4.9-closing-megaudit-codex.md:312:## 2. Non-goals (deferred)
docs/audits/2026-05-16-phase-4.8.G.3-closing-megaudit-codex.md:2393:docs/audits/2026-05-15-phase-4.9-closing-megaudit-codex.md:463:| 3 | **4.9.C parser** (W5-139, shipped) + **4.9.C binder** (W5-140, shipped) | **Parser (W5-139):** `Token::R1C1Ref` → intermediate `Expr::R1C1Ref { sheet, row_axis, col_axis }` (new variant) + `RangeRef::R1C1Cells` for ranges. Per-axis mixed-relativity check rejects with `ParseError::R1C1MixedRelativity`. Refined the design wording "Expr::CellRef with intermediate markers" to a new variant — keeps the 50+ `CellAddr` construction sites untouched. **Binder (W5-140):** `bind_with_context_v2` lowers `Expr::R1C1Ref` → `ExprPlan::CellRef { sheet, row, col, abs_col, abs_row }` using `BindSite::at_cell` for relative axes. Absolute axes drop straight in as `n - 1` (0-indexed). Relative axes resolve against `site.cell` (None → `BindError::R1C1RequiresAnchor`). Out-of-grid resolution → `BindError::R1C1OutOfBounds { resolved_row, resolved_col }`. The `abs_col` / `abs_row` flags on the emitted `ExprPlan::CellRef` are derived per-axis from the `AxisSpec` variant — preserves the abs/rel distinction the printer needs at 4.9.D. **Range lowering deferred** — `RangeRef::R1C1Cells` still surfaces via the existing `Expr::RangeRef(_)` `UnsupportedVariant` path (same as absolute `RangeRef::Cells`); range binding is handled by the existing aggregate-function dispatch and will fold R1C1Cells when that wave touches it. Calcgraph + printer `unreachable!()` stubs unchanged: storage canon (§ 4.4) lowers R1C1 → A1 text before fingerprint / stripe registration. |

docs/audits/2026-05-16-phase-4.8.G.3-closing-megaudit-codex.md:2583:docs/audits/2026-05-15-phase-4.9-closing-megaudit-codex.md:6430:docs/architecture/2026-05-15-r1c1-locales-implicit-intersection.md:177:| 3 | **4.9.C parser** (W5-139, shipped) + **4.9.C binder** (W5-140, shipped) | **Parser (W5-139):** `Token::R1C1Ref` → intermediate `Expr::R1C1Ref { sheet, row_axis, col_axis }` (new variant) + `RangeRef::R1C1Cells` for ranges. Per-axis mixed-relativity check rejects with `ParseError::R1C1MixedRelativity`. Refined the design wording "Expr::CellRef with intermediate markers" to a new variant — keeps the 50+ `CellAddr` construction sites untouched. **Binder (W5-140):** `bind_with_context_v2` lowers `Expr::R1C1Ref` → `ExprPlan::CellRef { sheet, row, col, abs_col, abs_row }` using `BindSite::at_cell` for relative axes. Absolute axes drop straight in as `n - 1` (0-indexed). Relative axes resolve against `site.cell` (None → `BindError::R1C1RequiresAnchor`). Out-of-grid resolution → `BindError::R1C1OutOfBounds { resolved_row, resolved_col }`. The `abs_col` / `abs_row` flags on the emitted `ExprPlan::CellRef` are derived per-axis from the `AxisSpec` variant — preserves the abs/rel distinction the printer needs at 4.9.D. **Range lowering deferred** — `RangeRef::R1C1Cells` still surfaces via the existing `Expr::RangeRef(_)` `UnsupportedVariant` path (same as absolute `RangeRef::Cells`); range binding is handled by the existing aggregate-function dispatch and will fold R1C1Cells when that wave touches it. Calcgraph + printer `unreachable!()` stubs unchanged: storage canon (§ 4.4) lowers R1C1 → A1 text before fingerprint / stripe registration. |

Out-of-grid resolution → `BindError::R1C1OutOfBounds { resolved_row, resolved_col }`. Calcgraph + printer `unreachable!()` stubs unchanged: storage canon (§ 4.4) lowers R1C1 → A1 text before fingerprint / stripe registration. |

docs/audits/2026-05-16-phase-4.8.G.3-closing-megaudit-codex.md:2682:docs/audits/2026-05-15-phase-4.9-closing-megaudit-codex-retry.md:1344:docs/audits/2026-05-15-phase-4.9-closing-megaudit-codex.md:6976:docs/audits/2026-05-15-phase-4.9-closing-megaudit-codex.md:829:./docs/architecture/2026-05-15-r1c1-locales-implicit-intersection.md:177:| 3 | **4.9.C parser** (W5-139, shipped) + **4.9.C binder** (W5-140, shipped) | **Parser (W5-139):** `Token::R1C1Ref` → intermediate `Expr::R1C1Ref { sheet, row_axis, col_axis }` (new variant) + `RangeRef::R1C1Cells` for ranges. Per-axis mixed-relativity check rejects with `ParseError::R1C1MixedRelativity`. Refined the design wording "Expr::CellRef with intermediate markers" to a new variant — keeps the 50+ `CellAddr` construction sites untouched. **Binder (W5-140):** `bind_with_context_v2` lowers `Expr::R1C1Ref` → `ExprPlan::CellRef { sheet, row, col, abs_col, abs_row }` using `BindSite::at_cell` for relative axes. Absolute axes drop straight in as `n - 1` (0-indexed). Relative axes resolve against `site.cell` (None → `BindError::R1C1RequiresAnchor`). Out-of-grid resolution → `BindError::R1C1OutOfBounds { resolved_row, resolved_col }`. The `abs_col` / `abs_row` flags on the emitted `ExprPlan::CellRef` are derived per-axis from the `AxisSpec` variant — preserves the abs/rel distinction the printer needs at 4.9.D. **Range lowering deferred** — `RangeRef::R1C1Cells` still surfaces via the existing `Expr::RangeRef(_)` `UnsupportedVariant` path (same as absolute `RangeRef::Cells`); range binding is handled by the existing aggregate-function dispatch and will fold R1C1Cells when that wave touches it. Calcgraph + printer `unreachable!()` stubs unchanged: storage canon (§ 4.4) lowers R1C1 → A1 text before fingerprint / stripe registration. |

docs/audits/2026-05-16-phase-4.8.G.3-closing-megaudit-codex.md:6545:docs/known-gaps.md:22:| GAP-R-07 | Phase 3.2 dep extraction loses the name when a `NameRef` resolves to `NamedTarget::Constant` or `NamedTarget::Cell` — the binder substitutes the value/CellRef and the source name does not appear in `ExprPlan` (so `CalcgraphSession::name_to_formulas` does not see it). Today the `PlanCache.name_gen` counter (Phase 2B.3) invalidates ALL formulas on any name mutation, so correctness is preserved; only the per-name precision is missing. Phase 3.3 wired `on_set_name` → `name_to_formulas`, which works for AggregateNameRef; this gap covers the scalar-NameRef precision miss that Phase 3.3 explicitly did NOT address. | `ql-exec/src/calcgraph_session.rs` module docs (§ "Still deferred"); `ql-exec/src/plan.rs::bind_with_names` scalar-NameRef branches | Engine | Engine Phase 4 (NameRef preservation in ExprPlan + binder revision) |
docs/audits/2026-05-16-phase-4.8.G.3-closing-megaudit-codex.md:8369:LOW: [workbook_runtime.rs](/Users/sanzhar/Documents/Sanzhar/Sanzhar/quantlab/quantlab-quantbook/quantbook-engine/crates/ql-exec/src/workbook_runtime.rs:2119) still says `resize_table` “does NOT dirty individual formula cells” and that `table_to_formulas` dirty propagation is “deferred.” That is now false after W5-159. Proposed fix: update the docstring to describe `reextract_table_readers` + `on_table_resize`.
docs/audits/2026-05-16-phase-4.8.G.3-closing-megaudit-codex.md:8371:LOW: [workbook_runtime.rs](/Users/sanzhar/Documents/Sanzhar/Sanzhar/quantlab/quantlab-quantbook/quantbook-engine/crates/ql-exec/src/workbook_runtime.rs:2309) still says resize cache clearing is a deferred targeted-invalidation substitute.
