docs/audits/2026-05-15-phase-4.9-closing-megaudit-codex.md:463:| 3 | **4.9.C parser** (W5-139, shipped) + **4.9.C binder** (W5-140, shipped) | **Parser (W5-139):** `Token::R1C1Ref` → intermediate `Expr::R1C1Ref { sheet, row_axis, col_axis }` (new variant) + `RangeRef::R1C1Cells` for ranges. Per-axis mixed-relativity check rejects with `ParseError::R1C1MixedRelativity`. Refined the design wording "Expr::CellRef with intermediate markers" to a new variant — keeps the 50+ `CellAddr` construction sites untouched. **Binder (W5-140):** `bind_with_context_v2` lowers `Expr::R1C1Ref` → `ExprPlan::CellRef { sheet, row, col, abs_col, abs_row }` using `BindSite::at_cell` for relative axes. Absolute axes drop straight in as `n - 1` (0-indexed). Relative axes resolve against `site.cell` (None → `BindError::R1C1RequiresAnchor`). Out-of-grid resolution → `BindError::R1C1OutOfBounds { resolved_row, resolved_col }`. The `abs_col` / `abs_row` flags on the emitted `ExprPlan::CellRef` are derived per-axis from the `AxisSpec` variant — preserves the abs/rel distinction the printer needs at 4.9.D. **Range lowering deferred** — `RangeRef::R1C1Cells` still surfaces via the existing `Expr::RangeRef(_)` `UnsupportedVariant` path (same as absolute `RangeRef::Cells`); range binding is handled by the existing aggregate-function dispatch and will fold R1C1Cells when that wave touches it. Calcgraph + printer `unreachable!()` stubs unchanged: storage canon (§ 4.4) lowers R1C1 → A1 text before fingerprint / stripe registration. |

Key decisions: keep `Value::Number(f64)` serial; 1900-default workbook-level date_system with 1904 alt; roll-our-own `ql-types::date` module; **new `ContextAwareFn` registry tier** (Codex HIGH 1) for date functions that need workbook context; sparse format-overlay + workbook-level `FormatTable` + 2 new op-log variants; serial-60 contract pinned per-function. 6 sub-phases planned (4.5.A.0 EvalContext tier, 4.5.A epoch+serial, 4.5.B 18-fn V1, 4.5.C 7-fn V2, 4.5.D format parser+storage+op-log, 4.5.E TEXT()+locale stubs) + mega-audit. docs/audits/2026-05-15-phase-4.9-closing-megaudit-codex.md:1704:./docs/architecture/2026-05-13-dates-times-formats.md:124:**Problem:** The W5-63 `RangeAwareFn` parallel-table pattern handled the "function arg is a range vs scalar" distinction. But Phase 4.5 introduces a NEW distinction: some functions need **workbook context** (date system, locale, now-provider). Under the current `fn(&[Value]) -> Value` signature, `DATE`, `DATEVALUE`, `WEEKDAY`, etc., have no way to read `Workbook::date_system`.
docs/audits/2026-05-15-phase-4.9-closing-megaudit-codex.md:1715:./docs/architecture/2026-05-13-dates-times-formats.md:455:- **Phase 4.9 R1C1 + localization**: format-string LOCALE lookup splits from RENDERING. Phase 4.5 hardcodes en-US; 4.9 swaps the lookup table in.
docs/audits/2026-05-15-phase-4.9-closing-megaudit-codex.md:1718:./docs/architecture/2026-05-13-coercion-matrix.md:24:The phase **NOT in scope for v1** is: dates / number formats / locale (Phase 4.5). The matrix's coercion rows assume invariant ASCII, no locale.
docs/audits/2026-05-15-phase-4.9-closing-megaudit-codex.md:1719:./docs/audits/2026-05-13-session-final-megaudit-sonnet.md:124:**W5-56 (`6c65fea5037`)** — CORRECT. Text functions use UTF-8 char-count semantics (documented divergence). FIND empty-needle returns start_num (Excel canon). SEARCH case-insensitive via `.to_uppercase()` char conversion is correct for ASCII/BMP but documented as deferred for locale-sensitive cases. REPT 32,767-char cap enforced. SUBSTITUTE empty old_text no-op is Excel canon.

docs/audits/2026-05-15-phase-4.9-closing-megaudit-codex.md:6430:docs/architecture/2026-05-15-r1c1-locales-implicit-intersection.md:177:| 3 | **4.9.C parser** (W5-139, shipped) + **4.9.C binder** (W5-140, shipped) | **Parser (W5-139):** `Token::R1C1Ref` → intermediate `Expr::R1C1Ref { sheet, row_axis, col_axis }` (new variant) + `RangeRef::R1C1Cells` for ranges. Per-axis mixed-relativity check rejects with `ParseError::R1C1MixedRelativity`. Refined the design wording "Expr::CellRef with intermediate markers" to a new variant — keeps the 50+ `CellAddr` construction sites untouched. **Binder (W5-140):** `bind_with_context_v2` lowers `Expr::R1C1Ref` → `ExprPlan::CellRef { sheet, row, col, abs_col, abs_row }` using `BindSite::at_cell` for relative axes. Absolute axes drop straight in as `n - 1` (0-indexed). Relative axes resolve against `site.cell` (None → `BindError::R1C1RequiresAnchor`). Out-of-grid resolution → `BindError::R1C1OutOfBounds { resolved_row, resolved_col }`. The `abs_col` / `abs_row` flags on the emitted `ExprPlan::CellRef` are derived per-axis from the `AxisSpec` variant — preserves the abs/rel distinction the printer needs at 4.9.D. **Range lowering deferred** — `RangeRef::R1C1Cells` still surfaces via the existing `Expr::RangeRef(_)` `UnsupportedVariant` path (same as absolute `RangeRef::Cells`); range binding is handled by the existing aggregate-function dispatch and will fold R1C1Cells when that wave touches it. Calcgraph + printer `unreachable!()` stubs unchanged: storage canon (§ 4.4) lowers R1C1 → A1 text before fingerprint / stripe registration. |
docs/audits/2026-05-15-phase-4.9-closing-megaudit-codex.md:6432:docs/architecture/2026-05-15-r1c1-locales-implicit-intersection.md:186:| 12 | **4.9.L** (W5-148, shipped) | Round-trip + edge case verification suite. +12 end-to-end property tests in `workbook_runtime::tests`: mixed-relativity range rejection at set_formula, `Sales[@Col]` vs `@Sales[Qty]` semantic equivalence, `@A:A` / `@1:1` whole-range narrowing at anchor, `Sheet1!@A1` cross-sheet, R1C1+EN round-trip through op-log replay (set_reference_mode + set_formula both replayed), DE+EN round-trip through replay, `@` preservation through replay, reference_mode/locale changes leave stored text canonical, `@scalar` idempotency, `@SUM(scalar args)` no-op. Note: rule 7 (function-returns-array → top-left) deferred — array-returning functions in scalar context still return `#CALC!` per existing 4.7.G limit; closing megaudit (4.9.O) decides whether to bundle that with cell-boundary spill rewiring or defer to a Phase 4.10 polish item. |

docs/compat/excel-matrix.md:120:| ROUNDUP | ⚠️ | 4 | 4.3 V1 | Round away from zero; sign-preserving. **Binary-float gotcha:** `ROUNDUP(0.1 + 0.2, 1)` rounds `0.30000000000000004` to `0.4`, while Excel's 15-digit display-aware rounding usually yields `0.3`. docs/compat/excel-matrix.md:123:| CEILING | ✅ | 4 | 4.3 V2 | W5-57: round away from zero to nearest multiple of significance. Default significance=1. Excel sign rule: number > 0 with significance < 0 → #NUM!. CEILING.MATH (mode flag) deferred. |
docs/compat/excel-matrix.md:124:| FLOOR | ✅ | 3 | 4.3 V2 | W5-57: round toward zero to nearest multiple. Same sign rule as CEILING. significance=0 with non-zero number → #DIV/0! (Excel canon — diverges from CEILING which returns 0). FLOOR.MATH deferred. |
docs/compat/excel-matrix.md:125:| CEILING.MATH | ✅ | 7 | 4.3 polish | W5-61: signature `(number, [significance], [mode])`. Significance is `abs(significance)` — sign ignored (unlike CEILING). Default significance=1, mode=0. Positive number always rounds toward +∞; negative number with mode=0 rounds toward +∞ (toward zero), with mode≠0 rounds toward -∞ (away from zero). significance=0 returns 0. CEILING.PRECISE deferred to 4.10. |
docs/compat/excel-matrix.md:126:| FLOOR.MATH | ✅ | 8 | 4.3 polish | W5-61: signature `(number, [significance], [mode])`. Mirror of CEILING.MATH. Positive number rounds toward -∞; negative+mode=0 toward -∞ (away from zero); negative+mode≠0 toward +∞ (toward zero). significance=0 + nonzero number → #DIV/0! (mirrors FLOOR canon, diverges from CEILING.MATH). FLOOR.PRECISE deferred to 4.10. |
docs/compat/excel-matrix.md:161:| LEFT / RIGHT / MID | ⚠️ | 9 | 4.3 V2 | W5-56: 1-based positions; UTF-8 char-count (UTF-16 canon deferred to a future Phase, same divergence class as LEN). Negative num_chars → #VALUE!; MID start < 1 → #VALUE!. |
docs/compat/excel-matrix.md:167:| CONCATENATE | ⚠️ | 4 | 4.3 V2 | W5-56: variadic scalar args, no range support (Excel CONCATENATE is the legacy non-range version). Errors propagate. CONCAT (range-aware variant) deferred to next batch. |
docs/compat/excel-matrix.md:176:| TEXT | ✅ | 28 | 4.5.E | W5-83: render Value via parsed Excel format string. Built on the W5-77→W5-82 format module (parser+renderer+FormatTable+overlay+runtime). Parse failures (incl. V2-deferred [Red]/conditionals/elapsed/fraction) surface as #VALUE!. Tests in `format::text_fn::tests` + `workbook_runtime::tests::text_formula_*` + e2e `format_persistence_round_trip_through_qbook`. |
docs/compat/excel-matrix.md:177:| VALUE | ✅ | 7 | 4.10.E | W5-167: parse text as number, locale-aware decimal separator (EnUs `.`; De/Fr `,`). ContextAwareFn. Trim whitespace; reject empty / non-numeric → #VALUE!. Numbers pass through; Blank → 0. **Strict locale-confusion guard**: in De/Fr locale, `.` in the numeric string → #VALUE! (closes ambiguity for "1.5" vs "1,5"). Currency prefixes + thousands grouping NOT parsed in V1; bundle with Phase 4.5 polish wave. |
docs/compat/excel-matrix.md:180:| DOLLAR | ✅ | 3 | 4.10.E | W5-167: currency text with `$` prefix. ContextAwareFn. Always groups thousands. Negatives → `-$1,234.50` (V1 — accounting parens + locale-specific currency symbol deferred to Phase 4.5 polish). |
docs/compat/excel-matrix.md:181:| CHAR / CODE | ✅ | 5 | 4.10.E | W5-167: codepoint round-trip for code 1..=255. **DIVERGENCE**: Excel uses Windows-1252; we use Unicode codepoint mapping. Identical for 1-127 ASCII; positions 128-159 differ (Windows-1252 has extra glyphs; Unicode has C1 control characters). Document divergence; bundle Windows-1252 polish with deferred UTF-16 work. |
docs/compat/excel-matrix.md:208:| XLOOKUP | ✅ | 10 | 4.10.G | W5-169: scalar-return V1. Modes: match_mode (0=exact, -1=exact-or-next-smaller, 1=exact-or-next-larger, 2=wildcard); search_mode (1=forward, -1=reverse, ±2=binary — V1 uses linear scan, same result, no perf advantage). `if_not_found` arg returned on miss (default `#N/A`). lookup_array must be 1D; 2D return_array → `#VALUE!` (spill semantics await Phase 4.7 polish). |
docs/compat/excel-matrix.md:210:| XMATCH | ✅ | 4 | 4.10.G | W5-169: modern MATCH variant. Returns 1-based position; same match_mode + search_mode semantics as XLOOKUP. No match → `#N/A`. |

codex
The financial code is a close IronCalc port for the TVM equations and IRR fallback, but one thing stands out: `RATE` claims the IronCalc loop and also divides by `rate` before any zero/near-zero guard, so an explicit zero guess can produce `#NUM!` instead of converging from a small perturbation or closed form.

  2862	    Value::Boolean(!matches!(args[0], Value::Text(_)))
  2863	}
  2864	
  2865	/// **W5-165:** `N(value)` — coerce to number per Excel canon:
  2866	/// - Number → same.
  2867	/// - Blank → 0.
  2868	/// - Boolean → 1 (TRUE) / 0 (FALSE).
  2869	/// - Text → 0 (NOT `#VALUE!` — Excel canon; verified against
  2870	///   IronCalc).
  2871	/// - Error → propagate.
  2872	///
  2873	/// Date values are stored as Number in this engine (no separate
  2874	/// `Value::Date` variant); dates round-trip through Number → N is
  2875	/// identity for date serials.
  2876	pub fn n_value(args: &[Value]) -> Value {
  2877	    if args.len() != 1 {
  2878	        return Value::Error(ErrorValue::Value);
  2879	    }
  2880	    match &args[0] {
  2881	        Value::Number(n) => Value::Number(*n),
  2882	        Value::Blank => Value::Number(0.0),
  2883	        Value::Boolean(true) => Value::Number(1.0),
  2884	        Value::Boolean(false) => Value::Number(0.0),
  2885	        Value::Text(_) => Value::Number(0.0),
  2886	        Value::Error(e) => Value::Error(*e),
  2887	    }
  2888	}
  2889

+// ===== W5-170 (Wave 2 closing megaudit MEDIUM-1) — fill e2e dispatch
+// gap for batches 4.10.E and 4.10.G. Unit tests covered the function
+// contracts; these prove the registry dispatch path works through the
+// lex/parse/bind/eval pipeline. =====
+
+#[test]
+fn e2e_char_code_basic() {
+    // =CHAR(65) → "A".
+    let result = eval_source_with_registry("CHAR(65)", &[]);
+    assert_eq!(result, Value::text("A"));
+    // =CODE("Z") → 90.
+    let result = eval_source_with_registry(r#"CODE("Z")"#, &[]);
+    assert_eq!(result, Value::Number(90.0));
+}
+
+#[test]
+fn e2e_unicode_unichar_basic() {
+    // =UNICODE("é") → 233.
+    let result = eval_source_with_registry(r#"UNICODE("é")"#, &[]);
+    assert_eq!(result, Value::Number(233.0));
+    // =UNICHAR(233) → "é".
+    let result = eval_source_with_registry("UNICHAR(233)", &[]);
+    assert_eq!(result, Value::text("é"));
+}
+
+#[test]
+fn e2e_value_basic_enus() {
+    // =VALUE("3.14") → 3.14 (default locale EnUs).
+    let result = eval_source_with_registry(r#"VALUE("3.14")"#, &[]);
+    assert_eq!(result, Value::Number(3.14));
+}
+
+#[test]
+fn e2e_fixed_default_format() {
+    // =FIXED(1234.567) → "1,234.57" (default decimals=2, EnUs locale).
+    let result = eval_source_with_registry("FIXED(1234.567)", &[]);
+    assert_eq!(result, Value::text("1,234.57"));
+}
+
+#[test]
+fn e2e_dollar_negative() {
+    // =DOLLAR(-1234.5) → "-$1,234.50".
+    let result = eval_source_with_registry("DOLLAR(-1234.5)", &[]);
+    assert_eq!(result, Value::text("-$1,234.50"));
+}
+
+#[test]
+fn e2e_textjoin_registered() {
+    // TEXTJOIN is RangeAwareFn; smoke-check via registry lookup.
+    let registry = default_registry();
+    assert!(registry.lookup_range_aware("TEXTJOIN").is_some());
+}
+

   325	/// Compare two `Value`s for equality per Excel's MATCH/VLOOKUP rule:
   326	/// text comparisons are case-insensitive; numbers and bools compare
   327	/// strictly; numeric-text DOES match the corresponding number (e.g.
   328	/// `Text("5")` matches `Number(5.0)` for lookup_value=5); Blank
   329	/// matches Blank only; Error never matches.
   330	fn lookup_eq(needle: &Value, hay: &Value) -> bool {
   331	    match (needle, hay) {
   332	        (Value::Error(_), _) | (_, Value::Error(_)) => false,
   333	        (Value::Blank, Value::Blank) => true,

   343	    }

  1437	/// Helper: coerce a single arg, truncate toward zero, require non-negative.
  1438	/// Returns the truncated `i64` value or an `ErrorValue` describing why.
  1439	fn coerce_nonneg_int(v: &Value) -> Result<i64, ErrorValue> {
  1440	    let n = match coerce_numeric(v) {
  1441	        NumericArg::Number(n) => n,
  1442	        // Blank → 0 (Excel canon for combinatoric args).
  1443	        NumericArg::Skip => 0.0,
  1444	        NumericArg::Error(e) => return Err(e),
  1445	    };
  1446	    let truncated = n.trunc();
  1447	    if truncated < 0.0 {
  1448	        return Err(ErrorValue::Num);
  1449	    }
  1450	    // Cap at i64 range; FACT/COMBIN overflow detection happens later.
  1451	    if truncated > i64::MAX as f64 {
  1452	        return Err(ErrorValue::Num);
  1453	    }
  1454	    Ok(truncated as i64)
  1455	}

- [scalar_fns.rs](/Users/sanzhar/Documents/Sanzhar/Sanzhar/quantlab/quantlab-quantbook/quantbook-engine/crates/ql-functions/src/scalar_fns.rs:1485): large combinatoric inputs can run effectively unbounded before returning overflow. `FACTDOUBLE(1e12)` loops until `k > n`; `COMBIN(n,n)` and `COMBINA(1, huge_k)` have similar risk. This violates bounded formula evaluation.  
  Fix: check finiteness during multiplication and return `#NUM!` immediately; use `k = min(k, n-k)` for `COMBIN`; add fast paths like `k=0`, `k=n`, `n=1`; add overflow boundary tests.

That fails the near-zero stability concern; Microsoft says RATE normally converges with guesses between 0 and 1, and zero is a natural user guess.
